films.title: 2026 Collide-O-Scope Halloween Show
films.description:
Collide-O-Scope’s Halloween celebration, a beloved Seattle tradition, returns from the beyondwith a one-of-a-kind found-footage phantasmagoria of hilariously hair-raising film freak-outsand outrageous oddball video! A deliriously demented cavalcade of expertly crafted montage,packed with absurd pop culture ephemera, obscure oddities, and awesome music — all remixedand mashed up into an evening of eerily epic entertainment. It’ll leave you gasping with laughterand clutching your little melted face! Plus, frightening fabulous prize drawings!

For over 16 years, Collide-O-Scope has been slaying Seattle audiences with their singular brandof entertainment, and their legendary Halloween extravaganza is not to be missed!

Costumes are encouraged, but there is no costume contest.

films.title: A Chinese Ghost Story
films.description:
The beloved cult classic fantasy, recently restored!

A traveling tax collector (Leslie Cheung) short on funds opts to take shelter in a seemingly abandoned temple. He is surprised to discover a young woman (Joey Wang) there and instantly falls for her beauty and grace. While every romance has its challenges, the tax collector gets more than he bargained for when he learns that the maiden is, in fact, a ghost... forced into servitude by a demon. With the help of a brave warrior, the tax collector must brave the perils of a supernatural world in order to free his newfound love.

Special live intro from local Hong Kong genre film connoisseur and one of the programmers of the Seattle Film Society, Patrick McFarland.

films.title: A Generation
films.description: Wajda’s striking feature debut, set in 1942 on the outskirts of occupied Warsaw, centers on Stach, a teen who witnesses his friend murdered by a Nazi and subsequently joins a left-wing resistance cell. The mixture of Italian neorealism and atmospheric dread established Wajda as a director to watch, as well as foregrounding key recurring themes in his work – honour, courage and sacrifice. The first in Wajda’s acclaimed war trilogy, this landmark film helped change the trajectory of Polish cinema with its stark account of wartime tragedies and coming of age during a time of unbelievable loss.

films.title: A Man and a Woman
films.description: This New Wave-style bitter-sweet romance took the world by storm, playing for a year and a half straight in Seattle. Persistence of emotional pain vies with the prospect of future happiness for an adult woman and man. Anne (Anouk Aimee, stunning and mysterious) works in the film industry and mourns her dead husband (Pierre: Pierre Barouh), killed in an accident. Jean-Louis (Jean-Louis Trintignant), a race car driver, lost his wife (Valérie Lagrange) to suicide. Chance brings Anne and Jean-Louis into proximity: her daughter and his son attend the same boarding school North in Deauville. There’s a spark between them, but what can come of it; they’re both in love with those who’ve departed. Writer-Director Lelouch engages us in Anne’s and Jean-Louis’ separate lives, thrillingly as he drives in the Le Mans and the Monte Carlo Rally races (Trintignant’s uncle won many races; for car aficionados: the film features Ford GT40s, early Mustangs). For Anne, her lost Pierre remains a felt presence, but she and Jean-Louis drive together in all weathers. They met by chance, and chance generates more suspense: are they really made for each other? Anouk Aimee is one of the screen’s enigmatic beauties, and Lelouch knows to enshrine her face: “It is women’s faces that speak.” What does she say?

films.title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
films.description:
1, 2, Feeddy's coming for you...

Nancy Thompson and her friends all share the same disturbing image in their dreams: a horribly disfigured man with knives on one hand. They soon learn this man is not just a figment of their imagination, and if they flal asleep, there's a very good chance they may never wake up.

Robert Englund plays the iconic Freddy Krueger in Wes Craven's horror classic. Heather Langenkamp stars as Nancy, one of cinema's most quintessential final girls. The film also features Johnny Depp's big screen debut as her boyfriend Glen.

films.title: A Serbian Film
films.description:
Co-presented with Scarecrow Video, keeping the world’s largest physical media archive alive, so no romance, no comedy, not even New French Extremity, is lost to time. Each Trauma Bond screening features a live Drag pre-show from Seattle’s own Monday Mourning.

An aging porn star agrees to participate in an “art film” in order to make a clean break from the business, only to discover that he has been drafted into making one of the harshest films ever made. In order to escape his living cinematic hell and save his family’s life, Milos will have to sacrifice everything – his pride, his morality, his sanity, and maybe even his own life.

films.title: A Simple Machine
films.description:
A Simple Machine is the award-winning, debut feature from director Mark Alan Hoffman, featuring a breakout lead performance by rising star Richard Blackmon. A true indie from the PNW, it is a quietly profound tour-de-force stunningly shot by cinematographer Kevin Fletcher (It’s What’s Inside) and scored by renowned composer Mark Orton (The Holdovers, Nebraska).

As the country looks to mark its 250th anniversary amid deep uncertainty, this story offers rare respite - a modern-day, cinematic Walden - a luminous, deeply human meditation on personal freedom, economic independence, and the cost of wanting less in a culture built on more.

“…relevant to almost everyone in America, as affordability becomes one of our biggest worries.” —Tim Molloy, MovieMaker

films.title: A. Rimbaud
films.description:
** Director Patrick Wang in-attendance for post-film Q&A**

The improbable life of French poet Arthur Rimbaud unfolds with all the shock and playfulness of his poetry.

films.title: Addams Family
films.description: The Addams Family is a fictional family and franchise created by American cartoonist Charles Addams. The Addams are an eccentric old-money clan who delight in the macabre and the grotesque and are seemingly unaware or unconcerned that other people find them bizarre or frightening. The family’s view in seeing their family life and interests as normal was a basis for the satire and comedy.

films.title: American Werewolf in London
films.description: After a terrifying encounter with a mysterious wolf in the English countryside, two American tourists are forever changed. One man dies from his injuries, while the other begins a horrifying transformation into a werewolf. He must confront the terrifying reality of his condition and the looming threat of the next full moon, all while being hunted by professionals determined to stop the savage beast he's becoming.

films.title: An Autumn Afternoon
films.description: The last film by Yasujiro Ozu was also his final masterpiece, a gently heartbreaking story about a man’s dignified resignation to life’s shifting currents and society’s modernization. Though the widower Shuhei (frequent Ozu leading man Chishu Ryu) has been living comfortably for years with his grown daughter, a series of events leads him to accept and encourage her marriage and departure from their home. As elegantly composed and achingly tender as any of the Japanese master’s films, An Autumn Afternoon is one of cinema’s fondest farewells.

films.title: Ashes and Diamonds
films.description: The final entry of Wajda’s celebrated WWII trilogy and a touchstone of Polish cinema, Ashes and Diamonds follows the militant Maciek (Zbigniew Cybulski) who finds himself tasked with the assassination of an incoming commissar. But when he falls for a local barmaid, he’s offered a glimpse of a world beyond war and destruction, leading him to question his commitment to a cause that risks his life. Wajda’s classic drama cemented his position as a world-class filmmaker and features an iconic central performance by Cybulski, the ‘Polish James Dean’ – who contributes legendary charisma to this probing look at the complex post-war future for a new nation and its people.

films.title: Band of Outsiders
films.description: Jean-Luc Godard returns from Contempt’s sun-splashed Mediterranean to Parisian black-and-white and the passion of his heart, his actress wife Anna Karina, the foremost icon of New Wave women. As in Breathless, Godard puts his appreciative-playful spin on Hollywood-style Noir. Two guys (Arthur: Claude Brasseur, Franz: Sami Frey), who perform pretend shoot-outs in the street, meet lovely, naive, doe-eyed Odile (Karina) at their English language class, where they break rules and pass notes to each other. There’s a stack of money hidden in the house where Odile lives, so why don’t they figure out how to steal it? Odile is less worldly than the men, but Karina conveys a woman growing into her exuberant selfhood. In a delightful sequence the three line dance the Madison for minutes of screen time. The men eventually tire and drop out, but smiling Odile keeps going, bouncing and snapping her fingers. Can these three pull off their robbery? They endearingly don’t seem up to it. There will be loaded guns, a dog’s breath cloud, the tallest ladder—and maybe a Hollywood ending. Godard and his master cinematographer Raoul Coutard make winter light and working class suburbs as richly flavorful as "Emily in Paris’s" picture postcard glamour. Going into Band of Outsiders, Anna Karina was at a personal low point; she says, “That film saved my life.” Quentin Tarantino loves this movie so much that he named his production company A Band Apart.

films.title: Basic Instinct
films.description:
The rock'n'roll drag duo Camp Napalm is back at Central Cinema, presenting the most iconic erotic thriller of the early 90s.

Catherine, a novelist with an insatiable sexual appetite, becomes a prime suspect when her boyfriend is brutally murdered in a fashion similar to a crime described in her latest story. San Francisco homicide detective Nick Curran is on the case, but starts to think Catherine probably didn't do it. Probably. At least he's sure enough to get sexually involved with Catherine and not feel bad about it. Except, what if his decision making skills are compromised by his attraction to Catherine? Given his history of making extremely poor professional choices, he's not sure what he's getting himself into, and Catherine may not let him get out of it alive.

Sharon Stone instantly became a household name thanks to her role as the provacative suspect Catherine, who is clearly the smartest person in any room she honors with her presence; she'll make you have feelings. Thankfully Camp Napalm will be on hand to help you process these feelings and rock your night with their live performances.

films.title: Beetlejuice
films.description: When a young couple dies and becomes trapped in their beloved home, they try to scare away the obtrusive new owners, the Deetzes. Their attempts backfire, inadvertently summoning Beetlejuice, a troublesome and chaotic ghost. Beetlejuice then inserts himself into the lives of the Deetzes and their teenage daughter, Lydia, creating escalating mayhem and comedic situations. The spirits must find a way to rid themselves of Beetlejuice before he ruins everything.

films.title: Begotten
films.description:
Easily one of the most singular films in the history of experimental cinema, E. Elias Merhige’s BEGOTTEN is a deeply religious, allegorical nightmare carved onto celluloid, distanced from recognizable place or time and uncovering a visceral, primitivist brutality that may be unparalleled in the history of the moving image.

Despite its near-total lack of cultural reference points, the churning, repetitive, symbolic actions of the entities depicted onscreen—all players from Merhige’s radical Theater of Material troupe—suggest a broad mythology drawn from sources as widespread as ancient Egyptian myth, disparate pagan traditions and Christian allegory. There is no dialogue or traditional narrative, yet BEGOTTEN’s hypnotic aesthetic and the ritualistic actions of its characters—named God Killing Himself, Mother Earth and Son of Earth, Flesh on Bone—are never anything but riveting.

And then there are the images. Merhige’s violently degraded black-and-white photography barely seems photographed at all: figures boil out of fields of grain, bodies dissolve into landscapes, and every frame flickers somewhere between an ancient cave painting, a damaged silent film and a transmission from a civilization that disappeared before history began. Watching BEGOTTEN can feel less like seeing a movie than witnessing some forbidden creation myth that has been dug out of the earth and projected for the first time. Beautiful, repulsive, hypnotic and genuinely otherworldly, it remains one of cinema’s great visions of a world being born and dying before your eyes.

“Evokes Alexander Sokurov and Francis Bacon as well as early David Lynch and a great many splatter films. If you’re looking to be freaked out you shouldn’t pass it up.” - Jonathan Rosenbaum

“One of the ten most important films of modern times.” - Susan Sontag

films.title: Bernstein's Wall
films.description: The barrier referred to in the title of this doc about musician Leonard Bernstein might first call to mind his ecstatic Christmas 1989 performances of "Beethoven’s Ninth" on both sides of what had been the Berlin Wall to celebrate its fall. These concerts marked the climax of the two intercrossing paths of his public life, music and social activism, but that wasn’t the only wall Bernstein faced—or, more accurately, crashed headfirst through. There was anti-Semitism: Orchestras welcomed Jews among their rank-and-file, of course, but their WASPy boards preferred WASPs on the podium. There were closet walls: Gay mentor Aaron Copland urged discretion, which for the effusive, voracious conductor was like urging tigers to go vegan. And most relevant to Bernstein’s legacy, there was the wall separating “high” from “low” culture, which he reduced to rubble. His classical training was traditional (Harvard, Curtis, and Tanglewood), but he also put together nightclub revues with his pals Judy Holliday and Comden & Green; cultivated an unprecedented TV presence as a peerless classical-music evangelist; and, most lastingly, wrote the score for probably the greatest of all musicals, “West Side Story” (which he composed concurrently with arguably the second-greatest, “Candide”). Appropriately for such a ravenous craver of the spotlight, Bernstein himself, rather than an array of talking heads, is just about the only speaker here; collaging TV interviews, home movies, and excerpts from sexually frank letters, director Douglas Tirola gathers the conductor’s own words into the nearest we’ll ever get to the memoir he never wrote. — Gavin Borchert

films.title: Black Zombie
films.description:
From the flickering screens of Hollywood horror to the haunted cane fields of colonial Haiti, BLACK ZOMBIE unearths the buried origins of the zombie, reclaiming it as a symbol of survival and spiritual resistance.

Long before it became associated with flesh-eating ghouls, the zombie was a living metaphor for slavery: not a monster, but the ultimate victim of colonial power. A symbol of stolen agency was recast as an object of fear, while Black spiritual traditions were distorted, sensationalized, and erased.

Director Maya Annik Bedward traces the evolution of the zombie, reconsidering iconic films like I Walked with a Zombie, Night of the Living Dead, White Zombie, and The Serpent and the Rainbow, alongside archival footage, vérité scenes, and interviews with cultural historians, artists, and genre legends including Yves-Grégory Francois, Mambo Labelle Déesse, Slash, Tom Savini, and Zandashé Brown. Part cultural reckoning, part horror remix, BLACK ZOMBIE exposes how a figure born from enslavement, spiritual belief, and resistance was transformed into one of pop culture’s most profitable monsters.

films.title: Blade
films.description:
Debate the cinematic value of superhero movies all you want, but the first successful Marvel adaptation holds up as a relentlessly entertaining example of how to make a movie from a comic book source.

Wesley Snipes is Blade, a bad-ass half-vampire on a mission to destroy the murderous bloodsuckers of the night. But the hunter becomes the hunted when forward thinking vampire Deacon Frost realizes that the sunproof Blade may be the key to resurrecting an ancient blood god.

Snipes brings a lot to the role thanks to his extensive martial arts training and swordsmanship, as well as his natural charisma. Stephen Dorff almost steals the show as the villaneous Deacon Frost. Definitely a film worthy of a trip to big screen.

films.title: Call Me By Your Name
films.description:
It's the summer of 1983, and precocious 17-year-old Elio Perlman is spending the days with his family at their 17th-century villa in Lombardy, Italy. He soon meets Oliver, a handsome doctoral student who's working as an intern for Elio's father. Amid the sun-drenched splendor of their surroundings, Elio and Oliver discover the heady beauty of awakening desire over the course of a summer that will alter their lives forever.

Part of the Rainbow Reels Series presented by SnoValley Pride (https://snovalleypride.org/).

films.title: Cameraperson
films.description: A boxing match in Brooklyn; life in postwar Bosnia and Herzegovina; the daily routine of a Nigerian midwife; an intimate family moment at home: these scenes and others are woven into Cameraperson, a tapestry of footage captured over the twenty-five-year career of documentary cinematographer Kirsten Johnson. Through a series of episodic juxtapositions, Johnson explores the relationships between image makers and their subjects, the tension between the objectivity and intervention of the camera, and the complex interaction of unfiltered reality and crafted narrative. A work that combines documentary, autobiography, and ethical inquiry, Cameraperson is both a moving glimpse into one filmmaker’s personal journey and a thoughtful examination of what it means to train a camera on the world.

films.title: Candy Mountain
films.description:
A rock ‘n’ roll odyssey from New York into the wilderness of Nova Scotia, Candy Mountain follows down-on-his-luck Julius, a generally unpleasant dude and mediocre musician to boot (Kevin J. O’Connor), who develops a get rich quick scheme: track down the reclusive guitar maker Elmore Silk. The journey up the road, full of wrong turns and dead ends, finds Julius confronting and frequently upsetting the disgruntled personalities that the ever elusive Silk left in his wake, from scorned family members (Tom Waits as Silk’s nouveau riche brother, a wheelchair-bound Dr. John as his cranky son in law) to abandoned lovers (Bull Ogier). Reportedly a challenging co-directorial collaboration, the film nonetheless registers as a delectable synthesis of Robert Franks photographic eye (as found in his canonical "The Americans") and the road mythologizing seen throughout the work of cult novelist Rudolph Wurlitzer (Two-Lane Blacktop, Walker, Pat Garrett And Billy The Kid). Spread out in the back seat for what Jonathan Rosenbaum calls a “wry, laid-back ‘Heart of Darkness.’”

35mm print courtesy of Museum of Fine Arts Houston.

films.title: Capturing Bigfoot
films.description: On October 20, 1967, Yakima-resident Roger Patterson and his friend Robert Gimlin captured 59 seconds of footage showing a hirsute creature walking through the Northern California woods, fifty miles north of Willow Creek. Known today as the Patterson-Gimlin Film, it would become one of the most analyzed and debated pieces of film in the history of the medium. Had Patterson and Gimlin proven the existence of the legendary cryptid known as Bigfoot? Despite charges of a hoax, Patterson never wavered in his claims to its authenticity, traveling around the country to exhibit it. After his untimely death in 1972, his widow and their family survived off of its licensing fees. Then, in 2024, a reel of 16mm film discovered in a safe changed everything—Clint Patterson, Roger’s son, embarked upon a search for the truth, uncovering long simmering grudges, buried secrets, and outright lies. Capturing Bigfoot reveals the untold story behind one of the world’s greatest mysteries as a son seeks to reconcile newfound facts with the memories of a beloved yet inscrutable father.

films.title: Carrie
films.description: Brian De Palma’s classic, supernatural horror film was based on Stephen King’s first novel and resulted in Sissy Spacek earning an Oscar nomination for her portrayal of a teenaged social outcast wielding fatal telekinetic powers. Carrie White (Spacek) is a shy, friendless teenager perpetually at the mercy of her Mean Girls-esque peers, who taunt and deride her on a daily basis. Her blind panic at her first menstruation—a result of her sheltered existence and the conservative, religious guilt drummed into her by her fanatical mother—only causes her classmates’ vicious harassment to escalate. Despite the well-intentioned interference of her protective gym teacher (Betty Buckley), Carrie’s fate as a bullying victim seems sealed. When Queen Bee Chris Hargenson (Nancy Allen) engineers a humiliating prank at the school prom, Carrie lashes out in a horrifying and vengeful display of her violent powers. One of the first mainstream films to focus on the special brand of cruelty unique to teenage girls, and a truly chilling horror film, Carrie endures as one of De Palma’s strongest achievements.

films.title: Cartoon Happy Hour
films.description: It's the Happiest Hour for the whole family! Two hours of classic cartoons to get your weekend started off right. We have kid friendly snacks and drinks. We also have adult friendly snacks and drinks! Every Thursday 5:00 until 7:00.

films.title: Casablanca
films.description: Academy Award winners Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman light up the screen in one of the most enduring romances in movie history--Casablanca. Rick Blaine (Bogart--The African Queen, The Caine Mutiny) owns a nightclub in Vichy-controlled Casablanca, frequented by refugees desperate to escape German domination. Despite the ever-present human misery, Rick manages to remain uninvolved in World War II now raging across Europe and Northern Africa. But all that changes when Ilsa Lund (Bergman--Gaslight, Notorious) walks through the front door of Rick's club--Rick must now choose between a life with the woman he loves and becoming the hero that both she and the world need.​

films.title: Castration Movie Chapter iii. Junior Ghosts—Premorphic Drift; a fragmentary passage
films.description: Castration Movie is a multi-part postmodern epic by visionary auteur Louise Weard. In Chapter iii. Junior Ghosts—Premorphic Drift, Izzy (Avalon Fast) seeks out everything in her power to stop her partner (Henri Gillespi) from transitioning.

films.title: CatVideoFest 2026
films.description: Oscilloscope Laboratories presents CatVideoFest 2026, a compilation of the latest and best cat videos culled from countless hours of unique submissions and sourced animations, music videos, and classic internet powerhouses. Each year, across the country, local theaters partner with nearby cat-focused charities, animal welfare associations and shelters alike — a portion of ticket proceeds from every show goes directly to local cats in need.

films.title: Chronovisor
films.description:
While writing a monograph on historical theories of memory, Béatrice (Anne-Laure Sellier), a respected academic, becomes beguiled by the allegedly true story of the Chronovisor, an occult device said to reproduce visuals from any point in history on a TV screen. Her obsession with the mysterious machine drags her from her Upper East Side apartment through the depths of New York City’s hidden libraries, to the edge of a breakthrough.

“Don’t miss CHRONOVISOR all hail CHRONOVISOR”

— Jane Schoenbrun (director, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma)

films.title: Clue
films.description: A group of strangers is invited to a remote mansion for a mysterious dinner party. When one of the guests turns up dead, the remaining attendees realize they're all suspects in a bizarre and comedic murder mystery. As they search for the killer, they uncover shocking secrets and unexpected twists, encountering familiar characters like Colonel Mustard, Miss Scarlet, and the astute butler, Wadsworth. The investigation is filled with laughter and suspense, keeping everyone guessing until the final, surprising reveal.

films.title: Come and See
films.description: This widely acclaimed film from Soviet director Elem Klimov is a stunning, senses-shattering plunge into the dehumanizing horrors of war. As Nazi forces encroach on his small village in present-day Belarus, teenage Flyora (Aleksei Kravchenko, in one of the screen’s most searing depictions of anguish since Renée Falconetti’s Joan of Arc) eagerly joins the Soviet resistance. Rather than the adventure and glory he envisioned, what he finds is a waking nightmare of unimaginable carnage and cruelty—rendered with a feverish, otherworldly intensity by Klimov’s subjective camerawork and expressionistic sound design. Nearly suppressed by Soviet censors who took eight years to approve its script, Come and See is perhaps the most visceral, impossible-to-forget antiwar film ever made.

films.title: Deep Red
films.description: The grisly killing of a celebrity telepath in Rome leads David Hemmings and Daria Nicolodi down a rabbit hole of repressed trauma, gruesome deaths and one of the creepiest puppets ever put on the screen. Dario Argento’s masterwork still feels incredibly modern; its perspective-shredding camera hurtles across rooms and lovingly circles fetishized instruments of both music and death while Goblin’s blissed-out prog-rock score blares on the soundtrack. Luxuriate in the rhythms of one of the most stylish thrillers ever made – here in its full, original Italian version. This is the movie that hooked every cinephile on the giallo genre.

films.title: Digger
films.description:
Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise in the title role.

The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

Cruise stars alongside Oscar winner Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Oscar nominee Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg, and Oscar nominee Jesse Plemons.

films.title: Dolphin Tale
films.description: After a young dolphin suffers a life-altering injury from a crab trap, a dedicated community rallies to rescue and rehabilitate her. Winter, a resilient and inspiring dolphin, faces an uncertain future with significant damage to her tail. A team of experts and a determined boy work together to develop an innovative prosthetic, leading to a remarkable recovery that captures the hearts of people worldwide and promotes hope and compassion

films.title: Dracula of Exarcheia
films.description:
A mad orthopedist arrives in Athens from the Carpathians, settles in the anarchist neighborhood of Exarcheia, and starts robbing graves for the body parts of dead musicians. His plan: stitch together the perfect rock band and make a fortune. Unfortunately, the dead have other ideas. Soon Athens’ militant zombies are organizing against the exploitation of their remains.

Part Hammer horror spoof, part punk-rock musical, part political satire and part document of the Greek underground at the dawn of the ’80s, Nikos Zervos’ gloriously disreputable cult oddity throws Frankenstein, Dracula, John Waters, socialist zombies, sexual anarchy and the real-life rock band Mousikes Taxiarhies into a blender. Tzimis Panousis leads a who’s-who of Greek counterculture through 87 minutes of passionate politics and absolute nonsense, culminating in a concert for the living and the dead.

A one-of-a-kind blast of Greek surrealism that has to be seen to be believed.

films.title: Dracula, Prisoner of Frankenstein
films.description:
Restoration by Severin Films

Jess Franco knows you know these monsters. He just wants to dream about them. So DRACULA, PRISONER OF FRANKENSTEIN wastes little time on introductions, explanations or even dialogue, and heads straight for the images that make monster movies irresistible. A castle looms through the fog. A coffin opens. Lightning flashes over a laboratory. Howard Vernon’s corpse-faced Dracula rises from the dead. Frankenstein’s Monster stalks the countryside. Beautiful women wander through the night. And just when the dream seems complete, the Wolf Man comes howling into it.

Dennis Price’s Dr. Frankenstein presides over this private Gothic universe, resurrecting and enslaving Dracula, commanding a homemade Monster of his own and sending everyone drifting through castles, crypts and desolate landscapes to Bruno Nicolai’s magnificent score. Franco lets plot dissolve into atmosphere and gives himself over to whatever image fascinates him next, his camera zooming compulsively toward faces, windows, animals and strange details in the landscape. Nothing needs to look realistic to feel uncanny here. A rubber bat is still a rubber bat, but when Franco sends it flapping across a real Gothic landscape, somehow the whole world gets stranger (and better).

This is Jess Franco in concentrated form: cheap and beautiful, crude and hypnotic, made in a hurry by a filmmaker who trusts his own obsessions more than the rules of conventional filmmaking. Part Universal monster rally, part comic book, part lost silent film in delirious color, DRACULA, PRISONER OF FRANKENSTEIN strips monster cinema down to the things Franco loves most and rearranges them according to the logic of a dream. Frankenstein looks handmade. The bat has a wire. The camera zooms like it’s possessed. The Wolf Man seems to have wandered in from another movie. And the whole thing is beautiful enough to bring tears to your eyes.

“The movie F.W. Murnau might have made if Universal had hired him to direct HOUSE OF FRANKENSTEIN in color." - Tim Lucas

films.title: Drawn to Life (Shorts)
films.description:
Frame by frame, this vibrant and hand-crafted program features animated and energetic stories brought to life with care and vision. These films artfully showcase the power of telling a story your own way, exploring transformation and identity in beautiful motion.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Ahyoka (Schon ᎤᎶᎩᎳ Duncan, United States, 13m)

A portrait of Ahyoka Youngdeer, Cherokee culture bearer, teacher, and two-spirit activist. Weaving her own life with a traditional Cherokee story about a crooked-face boy, Ahyoka traces how exclusion was never a Cherokee value and reminds us what it truly means to be a Keetoowah person.

ANADROMOUS (Ari Grubb, United States, 5m)

When they find themselves evolving out of their aquarium home, two fish set off on a musical journey of self-acceptance and queer joy, and find community in a freaky fish gay bar in the deepest depths of the ocean.

Bright Eye (Rio Miller, Canada, 21m)

Callie Jones is not your average IT tech. They’re a bio-hacker, living in the cracks of their dystopian society and illegally hacking bionic implants. Careful. Methodical. Invisible… until one wrong phone call exposes them.

CW: Flashing lights

Eve (Jesse Kogita, United States, 13m)

“Eve” is a short animated film based on the autobiographical stories of transitioning by Eve Palay, a trans woman living in the Pacific Northwest.

Eyeliner (Aisha Boudjillouli, United Kingdom, 8m)

Nina and her best friend Lily decide to steal an eyeliner, hoping that this will be their key to womanhood. When they’re given wildly different receptions, Nina discovers her journey as a trans girl might not be so easy.

CW: Transphobia

I HAVE BECOME (Lee J Holoubek, Canada, 1m)

A paint-on-paint + risograph queer experimental animation about a transgender man’s relationship with his body, younger self, and future self to show the grotesque beauty of tearing oneself apart to live truthfully.

CW: Flashing lights

Las Cosas Que Brillan (Kristal Sotomayor, United States, 11m)

Using a combination of liveaction with handbuilt foamboard sets and puppetry, a curious trans mermaid defies her mother’s warnings to venture up to the surface, only to discover the world above is not what she dreamt.

Promise Me (Gilda Panizza, Italy, 3m)

“Promise me” is a spell, a call and response where the one who asks and the one who answers blur into each other, using ink to build cyborg bodies the subjects imagine for themselves

SunKissed Sapphics (Jennifer Marie Cella, United States, 8m)

Three transgender lesbians, all represented as endangered species, happen to meet in a hotel lobby. The trio embark on a passionate and psychedelic odyssey across the south Jersey boardwalk.

films.title: Driller
films.description:
An X-rated horror musical inspired by Michael Jackson’s THRILLER, starring Taija Rae and a pop superstar named Mr. J. DRILLER could only have happened in 1984—and even then, somebody really had to want to make it.

Adult-film veterans and lifelong horror fans Joyce James and Timothy Green Beckley wanted to make something different, and the enormous cultural impact of THRILLER gave them their way in. Taija Rae plays Louise, an obsessed fan whose fascination with Mr. J carries her from a pop concert into a handmade Gothic nightmare. What begins as an unmistakable riff on Jackson and John Landis gradually wanders deeper into horror-movie territory, with original songs, choreography, transformation effects and smoky monster-movie atmosphere assembled with the resources and ingenuity of an independent adult production.

The distance between THRILLER’s Hollywood spectacle and DRILLER’s lovingly threadbare recreation is part of its charm, but James never treats the idea as a throwaway joke. She commits to it, building the parody into a strange little world with a personality entirely its own.

More than forty years later, DRILLER remains a perfect artifact of its moment: Golden Age adult filmmaking colliding head-on with MTV, the early-’80s horror boom and the biggest music video on Earth. Rough, playful and wildly ambitious, it’s the work of filmmakers who wanted to make something unusual and followed that impulse much further than anyone could reasonably have asked. There is only one DRILLER.

Founded by the Seattle Erotica Cinema Society in 2016, SECS Fest celebrates a diverse range of sexually explicit representations, finding beauty in erotic difference and inspiring adult conversations about sex.

Dedicated to bringing world-class erotic movies to Seattle screens all year, SECS Fest is also delighted to partner with The Beacon for a series of monthly screenings, leading up to the 2026 edition of SECS Fest in November! For more info, see: https://www.secsfest.org/

films.title: Elvira: Mistress of the Dark
films.description: A mysterious inheritance brings horror hostess Elvira to the most uptight town imaginable, where pearl-clutching locals and a dangerously low neckline collide in one of the silliest and spookiest camp comedies ever conjured.

films.title: Engauge 2026 – Beyond Borders
films.description:
This seemingly disparate collection of films takes us beyond the often artificial boundaries of countries, equipment, formats, frames, genres, species, states, and styles.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Some Place to Stand (Sandy McLennan | color/sound | 16mm to digital | 4:04 | CA)

An Expo ’67 song on 45, current hand-processed film footage, reflecting on social concepts then and now.

The Spider (Shanna Maurizi color/sound | 16mm to digital | 8:45 (time updated?) | US)

Nighttime visions emerge from a dusty roadside and out of the depths of the subconscious as two characters are drawn together by a shared experience. “The Spider” mines family history by developing an ancestral mythology where time is simultaneous, but loss is real.

Hurricane Season (Michelle Trujillo | b&w/sound | 16mm to digital | 6:22 | US)

Hurricane anxiety takes a visceral form as the image searches for an escape route. Inspired by true events. Created on 16mm film and developed with comfrey, mint, yerba mate and willow leaves.

Jonah (Daniel Cortés Ramírez | b&w/sound lomokino to digital *wide* | 10:40 | Colombia)

Jonah, the anti-prophet, escapes once again from the god who humiliated him.

He boards a ship to Tarshish, and out on the vast sea, a distant yet familiar echo calls to him. His body trembles from the trauma, but a deep embrace gathers him up and holds him close.

This film uses 35mm Lomokino footage to imagine an alternative fate for the perpetrators’ violence.

En La Paz (Jeremy Moss | b&w/sound | 16mm to digital | 3:00 | US/Bolivia)

Created in-camera on a rooftop in La Paz, Bolivia in July on B&W reversal film with my Bolex as dusk was approaching. The city’s sea of antennas and surrounding mountains pointing to the sky inform the film’s sound.

Kaze No E (or Why the Wind Whispers Among the Leaves) (Takahiro Suzuki | color/sound | 16mm to digital | 7:05 | US)

Four young researchers in Big Sky Country begin to wonder about the vastness of the world and greater cosmos. If non-human presences were capable of harboring intelligence and communicating, what information could they pass along? Using the trees and wind as messengers, the researchers record and decipher writings and recordings from the trees and wind, relating them back to the land and universe, before finding ways to embody them through sound and movement as a form of empathy and communion with a greater intelligence.

Transmission (Douglas Urbank | b&w/sound | 16mm to digital | 7:20 | US)

Layers of patterns generate sound.

Toss a Rose Over (Janelle VanderKelen | color/sound | 16mm to digital | 10:44 | US)

The green ones share stories of change in this travelogue from the vantage point of plants. In a canyon where all things move, these ancient beings urge humanity to reconsider acts of interspecies and intraspecies relation during a current period of anthropogenic climate change.

Leaf Peeper (Vito Rowlands | color/sound | Super 8 to digital | 2:54 | US)

A frantic frolic in Fall foliage. A stop-motion autumn adventure. A symphony in blaze orange.

Run (Robert Schaller | b&w/silent | 11:51 | 16mm print | US)

An optical quest to capture the feeling of running through the Colorado mountains on and around the Continental Divide.

Alpine Tundra (Kathleen Rugh | color/sound | 5:35 | 16mm print | US)

At an elevation of 14,264 feet above sea level, the peak of Mount Blue Sky is too harsh for trees and common vegetation. Instead, the ground is covered with fragile tundra grass, weak soil, and rock. In this harsh climate exists the highest paved road in North America, that allows visitors traveling by car to partake in striking views and a sense of awe in the extremes of nature.

films.title: Engauge 2026 – Expanded Cinema Performance and Film
films.description:
FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

No Landscape Ever Made Me Cry (Sujin Lee | b&w/silent | 5:30 |16mm to digital | US/Korea)

I am a crier, and this film tells stories about holding back (or not holding back) tears; words break down and often turn into crying. The film tries to explain those tears. It also reflects an ambivalent attitude—being personal while trying to maintain distance from these emotions, wanting to talk about crying but not quite being able to. Produced on 16mm film using inkjet-printed paper and plastic negatives, the entire process was cameraless.

Pedra e Montanha, Expanded Cinema Performance of 35mm Slides by Tetsuya Maruyama (3-35mm slide projectors + live sound accompaniment by Corey J. Brewer | 50:00 | Brazil)

A continuation of ongoing research into contemporary mining activities in Brazil and beyond. Multiple 35mm slide projectors cycle through images captured by a Brazilian mining company while being manipulated live by the artist using three 35mm slide projectors. Live sound accompaniment by local artist/musician Corey J. Brewer incorporates field recordings taken by Maruyama and Brewer (check for accuracy).

films.title: Engauge 2026 – Pattern and Place
films.description:
Inspired by Eric Stewart’s description of his film as “a quiet study in pattern and place,” these films closely observe phenomena, not limited to but often privileging the natural world. 2 films will be shown on 16mm and the last is an expanded cinema performance.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Maya at 24 (Lynne Sachs | b&w/sound | 4:47 | 16mm to digital | US)

Lynne Sachs films her daughter Maya in 16mm black and white film, at ages 6, 16 and 24. At each iteration, Maya runs around her mother, in a circle – clockwise – as if propelling herself in the same direction as time, forward. Conscious of the strange simultaneous temporal landscape that only film can convey, we watch Maya in motion at each distinct age.

Solar Wave (Christina Nguyen | color/sound | 2:53 | 16mm to digital | US)

sun light, sun set, sun rise, sun ray. a hand processed in camera roll shot on Kodak 3383 color print stock.

Hemispheres (Eric Stewart | color/sound | 7:14 | 16mm to digital | US)

Filmed over the course of several years in southern Colorado, Hemispheres is a quiet study in pattern and place, as observed through the window of my living room. Shot on Super 16mm film, the project layers multiple time-lapse exposures of cacti and seasonal light, capturing subtle shifts in color, atmosphere, and rhythm. Like the inlay of a sundial meeting a garden’s creeping vines, what emerges is not a photograph of a singular view or moment, but a composite drawing of duration—using light to trace the intersecting cycles of growth and dormancy, brightness and shadow, warm and cool, seasonal progression and retreat…

Stock (Lucy Ellis | color/sound | 1:50 | 35mm to digital | UK)

Stock uses both new and obsolete digital stock imagery transferred onto 35mm film through UV printing, pen plotting and sticker transfer. Drawing parallels between the vertical storage of information digitally and on the film surface, the imagery transfers from one storage system to another allowing for a shift in line, texture and detail, a drift from digital precision. Undertaking a new form of light and a new identity (from digital to analog) the imagery becomes slow in its formation whilst unstable in nature.

Licht & Ton (Light & Sound) (Jan Rehwinkel | b&w/sound | 5:50 | Germany)

A film without a camera: The fascination of painting tone or noise—a composition of visible sound and audible images. After experimenting with photograms on 16mm film, whose technical precision proved too much for me, I decided to switch to what I like best about filmmaking: painting what I want to see (and hear!) onto the material myself. When I work this way, I am constantly confronted with failure or the impossibility of perfection – even the contact printer I used to make the screening copy was unpredictable. But I see all of this as a creative tool and integrate it into the process.

Fluss (Penny McCann | b&w/sound | 3:39 | 16mm to digital | CA)

In this experimental film, a journey down the Danube River is transformed into a dream space of half-seen images and flickering shorelines. Though at times abstract, the river remains certain, always moving towards the sea. Filmed in black and white 16mm and hand-processed, Fluss is a companion to River (2023), a black and white study of the Ottawa River in winter. Commissioned by Ottawa’s Lightproof Film Collective.

Drift (Tessa Garland | b&w&color/sound | 7:25 | S 8 to digital | UK)

Shot on Super 8, the film captures a walk around a precarious, low-lying sandbank island, where fleeting observations come into focus only to vanish again. Rotations and cycles ebb and flow through manmade wind vanes assembled from foraged sea drift, while sea-worn objects hint at deeper meanings beneath the surface. Prehistoric-looking cacti punctuate the island, contributing to its strange, otherworldly atmosphere.

Phytophonics (Karel Doing | color/sound | 4:18 | 16mm to digital | UK)

Plant matter is used to create finely detailed indexical traces on photochemical film. The traces are not only visible but also audible. By feeding botanical textures, patterns and rhythms into the optical sound system noise, cracks, pops and hiss is generated. Seeing is hearing. Such a cross modality disobeys the usual lipsync illusion and replaces this so called realism with a radically different concreteness. Phytophonics is serious play with living material in a world that is increasingly based on simulated sham. Eco-punk against the abyss created by late-capitalism.

Spring Song (Wei Gao | color/sound | 16:21 | 16mm to digital | Korea/France)

“Spring Song” was filmed from 2016 to 2024. Every spring, the filmmaker, armed with a Super 8mm camera and using the vibrant colors of Ektachrome super 8 film, or Kodak color negative film, captured the vibrant blossoms, grasses, leaves, insects, and small animals of spring. The filmmaker’s meticulous daily observations in her own rooftop garden, as well as her chance encounters in the National Forest Park, revealed a rich natural ecosystem. She also employed cameraless photography, creating images of plants through photochemical reactions between Super 8mm film, plants, and organic matter. She then combined these Super 8mm and cameraless images together to create a dynamic and colorful vision of spring. In the context of increasingly strained ecological environments, the director created a living green ecosystem in her rooftop garden, observing plants and practicing a lifestyle integrated with nature.

Gradually Forming a Circle (Zack Parrinella | color/sound | 8:02 | 16mm print | US)

A stepped and steady progression of a line becoming a circle. Soundtrack by Zekarias Musele Thompson.

The Rocks: Kata Tjuta West of Ularu (Dianna Barrie and Richard Tuohy | color/sound | 6:00 16mm print | AU)

Looking at the present, as though the far future were dreaming of its ancient past – an ‘iconogenic’ vision of Australia.

Mounds Above the Earth (Jaiyi Chen | color/sound | 7:39 | *35mm, 16mm and interventionist tools, performed by Spencer Sundell | US)

“Mounds Above the Earth” contemplates ecological cycles, perception, and environmental transformation, anchored in the rare emergence of two periodical cicada broods surfacing simultaneously for the first time in more than two centuries. The film follows the flicker of red through the cicadas’ developing eyes, a blood moon, and a retelling of an ancient fable.

films.title: Engauge 2026 – Tactility and Memory
films.description:
These films posit a connection between the haptic world and what we choose to embody, remember, erase, perhaps forget. Filmmakers manipulate the medium in a variety of ways to emphasize visual texture and showcase techniques that evoke memory and touch.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Caribou (Lindsay Aksarniq McIntyre | color/sound | 16mm to digital | 15:00 | CA)

An experimental documentary created with handmade and manufactured emulsions exploring the close and enduring connections between Inuit, caribou, lichens, and land use. Lichen developers help bring the images to life, while caribou hide is processed into gelatin to make handmade emulsion. Filmed primarily on the land in Nunavut where caribou struggle to maintain their lifeways amidst burn events, habitat disruption and changing conditions.

I Found Some Old Footage of a Tree (Krista Lee Steinke | color/sound | 16mm to digital | 3:22 | US)

An experimental film that unfolds as a glimpse into the creative process: a sketch, a vignette, a visual mind map, and a meditation on how to document a planet in flux. In this piece, the materiality of film becomes a metaphor for time, impermanence, and the fragility of the natural world. Working with Super 8mm and 16mm footage, the image itself carries traces of transformation, decay, and memory, blurring the boundaries between document and artifact. A sense of anxiety and urgency shapes the work, leaving us uncertain whether we are witnessing the past, the present, or a message from the future. Ultimately, the film asks how cinema can hold onto a world that is continually changing, and what remains when both landscapes and images begin to disappear.

EOJ (Tianming (Alaric) Zhou b&w/sound | 16mm to digital | 2:22 | China/US)

Regulatory signs shot on 16mm, hand-processed with caffenol, and subjected to both analog and digital corrosion. EOJ reimagines the anxiety induced by caffeine hypersensitivity and the pressures of social conditioning.

Autopsia del Río (Ada Rajkovíc | color/sound | Super 8 to digital | 2:37 | US)

Inspired by David Gatten’s “What The Water Said,” this film uses the material of Super 8 celluloid itself to record the memories of the Río de la Plata, a former burial ground for los desaparecidos during Argentina’s military dictatorship.

Flow Attachment (Tijana Petrovic | b&w/sound | 16mm to digital | 8:40 | US)

A coastal sand dune is transformed and reshaped into digital ether. The film focuses closely on sand as a material, which is composed of silica, the mineral that is a primary ingredient in manufacturing silicon chips, lenses, binoculars, microscopes and mirrors – devices that extend our vision. The film uses these devices to visually capture the sand dune and evoke the transformation of materials that goes into their production. Through 16mm analog techniques, elemental forces of a sand dune merge with the physical properties of the celluloid.

Polychora (Abinadi Meza | color/sound | 16mm to digital | 9:22 | US/Mex)

A cameraless 16mm film, scanned to 4K and slowed into extreme temporal dilation: an aqueous prism where chromatic membranes evolve. Its title evokes the polychoron, a four dimensional form. Fractal traces surface within the color fields: analog and digital, cellular and cosmic, coexisting in the same luminous space. Polychora functions as a neuro refuge, a haptic cinema where the eyes and body can rest inside something vast.

Tactile Light Diary (Callon Murphy | b&w/sound | 8mm to digital | 6:00 | CA)

Touch replicated through audiovisual means./Fabric structures exposed and magnified.

Textiles dance over microphone and screen./Images burst to the forefront.

First a beach, then an unclean pool./Summer slips into fall./ Details are forgotten or misremembered./The retained memory of tactile objects.

Need and Desire (Francesca Svampa | color/sound | Super 8 to digital | 8:24 | Spain/Italy)

A gesture of erasure. A spell. If you lift the emulsion from a photograph, destroy its surface, transplant it onto a new body, does the memory it carried survive? “Need and Desire” originates from this question, and from the poetic belief that making a film can alter reality. The cinematic act becomes [an] incantation: a process that destroys and reconstructs simultaneously. Still memories become an “emulsional” landscape.

Fata Morgana (Hannu Nieminen | color + b&w/sound | Super 8 to digital | 5:16 | Finland)

Fata Morgana is a mirage phenomenon in which distant objects appear distorted, often floating or stretched out on the horizon. The film is an experimental study of memory, images and filming, and how memories can transform, rust and disintegrate. The photographs are from a summer spent on the banks of the Terijoki River in Karelia, which [the] Soviet Union took from Finland after WWII.

Interwoven Intervals (Laura Kraning | b&w/sound | 16mm to digital | 6:00 | US)

Pattern drafts are the graphical score for weaving – grids of light and dark representing the over and under of weft threads between the warps. In this material hybrid of film and textile, the graphic repetition of grids, lines, and squares assert a structural form that is fragile and vulnerable to erasure.

La Duréte du Mental/Mental Toughness (Charles-Andre Coderre | color/sound | 35mm to digital *wide* | 20:00 | CA)

“It’s a distraction for many, a profession for a few, when for me sport is my whole life. And if fighting is the reason you’re living. If every muscle clamors : train me, exercise, put on a sprint. Find a competitor or at least fight against a pole. It’s hard to get started but it’s otherwise difficult to stop. Even with your back against the mat. Never mind. You have to stand up and go further. You will now have to fight against yourself.” Transforming Olympic wrestling and pole vaulting Soviet films from the 1980s into expressive, painterly imagery, the film appears as a film practitioner’s decathlon.

films.title: Engauge 2026 – Tainted
films.description:
This program gathers a group of films that confront the various underbellies of life: deceptive icons, devastated landscapes, climate change, predatory advertising, drug addiction, toxic politics and environmental disasters, among others, using found footage emulsion lifting, documentary techniques, handmade film and cameras, single framing, and narrative strategies.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Front Ear Theory (Brady Lewis | color/sound | 5:12 | S8 to digital | US)

“Front Ear Theory” is a five-minute history lesson. To be more precise, it’s a story about a history lesson. Or about a history teacher. It’s an experimental narrative that was shot entirely on super-8 (mostly Kodachrome) film.

Bigger Than Us, The Berkeley Pit, Butte, Montana (color/sound | 9:00 | 16mm to digital | US)

A portrait of a huge open-air copper mine in Butte, Montana. The closed mine dominates the city geographically, and also financially, culturally, historically, and in the on-going health effects from the highly toxic metals and chemicals which fill the bright blue-green water in the pit. (The pit is a designated Superfund site.) After a few opening titles which briefly introduce us to the pit and its history, the film becomes a wordless visual montage, almost always superimposing several layers of footage.–David Finkelstein.

Blu/Blue (Andrea Nevi | color/sound | 4:47 | Super 8 to digital | Italy)

A community displaced by a climate disaster settles in a new habitat, where memories of their former way of life slowly begin to resurface. BLU is an experimental climate fiction short film made entirely from Super 8mm found footage recovered from a flea market.

Injured? (Eislow Johnson | color/sound | 13:28 | 16mm to digital | US)

Need help? Crashouts, manifestation influencers and injury lawyers collide in this breakneck ride through the Midwest. 50 years after attorney ads were first legalized in the U.S., their ubiquitous self-portraits (allegedly) invoke a churn-and-burn economy of volume, velocity, fears and veneers.

What You Don't See (Karl Nussbaum | color/sound | 1:25 | 16mm to digital | US)

This film is about what the audience doesn’t see when we watch a film – the sprockets, the optical soundtrack, the splicing tape, the celluloid itself, the frame lines, etc. This is a very short Direct Animation film I made at MONO NO AWARE in Brooklyn. It’s totally analog and was made using only 16 mm and Super 8 found footage film strips.

On The Glue (Dave Johnson | color/sound | 3:02 | 16mm to digital | CA)

From the depths of London, England’s Barracks district amongst the derelict weapons huts, comes a public service expose from the 1970s revealing “THE HORRORS” of kids participating in the act of glue sniffing. The narrative is told in three parts: The reporter, a mother, and her “addict son” David. This film and its title have been appropriated from a 1970’s BBC expose. The visual treatment exposed the footage (and the filmmaker) by gluing pieces of film together then ripping it apart. This becomes an interesting metaphor of creating using the substance of the problem presented in the film. The film was edited by hand and sequenced using measurements to time each shot.

The Gloaming (Charlotte Pryce | color/sound | 14:00 | 16mm to digital | US)

A metaphorical tale of pyrophytic transmutation, of metamorphosis through fire. Inspired by medieval paintings of celestial portents, The Gloaming is a work of bio-mysticism that takes the form of a fable. The slippage between substances and the ethereal nature of matter finds a parallel in the chemical accretions of the hand processed film. In a time of environmental uncertainty, the film offers a story of adaptation and survival.

Thought/Action (Dirk De Bruyn | color/sound | 10:27 | 16mm to digital | AU)

Initiated in 1996 and belatedly completed in 2026, this home-processed 16mm film material was inspired by Marc Adrian’s Total (1968) and incorporates Moucle Blackout and Laszlo Dudas’s voices. Partially shot at Hearst’s San Simeon Castle, Canada and Royal Melbourne Show, it is an exploration of overcoming traumatic thoughts through materialist actions onto the film surface. The completion gap demonstrates the power of and resistance to traumatic events.

Better Lighting (Kathryn Ramey | color/sound | 2:13 | 16mm to digital | US)

An agitprop made from two 30-second GE adverts from the 1970s repurposed to rebuke the role white women voters in the US have chosen to uphold white supremacy and the patriarchy instead of supporting the interests of women and anyone who loves them.

Necropolis (Kevin T. Allen | color/sound | 8:53 | Super 8 to digital | US)

A Stone Tape film inspired by the yellow fever epidemic in 19th century New Orleans, using analog camera techniques and contact microphones to excavate the material traces of trauma. Coined by archaeologist and parapsychologist T.C. Lethbridge, Stone Tape Theory posits that material objects record traumatic events of the past…and that they can be played back.

Good Neighbors Care (Kate E. Hinshaw | color/sound | 3:50 | 16mm to digital | US)

For decades chemical company DuPont and its subsidiary Chemours poisoned North Carolina’s drinking water through illegally dumping forever chemicals into the Cape Fear River. On altered 16mm film, corporate promises of community care and pure water dissolve as rivers and bodies merge in a meditation on what it means to exist in an imperfect environment.

North (Hogan Seidel | b&w/sound | 3:00 | 16mm to digital | US)

I found a decaying print of Nanook of the North and continued its collapse through photochemical processes, confronting the violence of its legacy. “North” is not a restoration, but a reckoning—an act of holding damaged images until they blur, bleed, and refuse the gaze that once claimed them.

Assets (Christine Lucy Latimer | color/sound | 2:22 | 16mm print | CA)

Hundreds of digitally generated filters and assets used by online content creators to simulate a “shot on film” aesthetic are collaged together on expired 16mm Ektachrome. Random contemporary approximations of film artifacts, ranging from industrial to experimental, move through the frame in impossible trajectories. A film of transitions that never transition, positioning moving image signifiers in a post-truth era.

Ashes to Ashes (Sidney Gordon | color/sound | 5:00 | 16mm print | CA)

“Ashes to Ashes” depicts fragments of the artist’s diary as they undergo physical and emotional transformation through a blazing agricultural landscape. Words turn to ash as the past is consumed by flames. Rivers ignite from embers, flow through vessels and begin to crack. Manifested through the land and material processes lies a situated reflection on recovery, loss and evolution. The film was shot at the 2024 Independent Imaging Retreat. It was developed with common comfrey and contaminated wood ash foraged from the farm and was coated in the artist’s blood.

films.title: Engauge 2026 – We Are All Together
films.description:
This phrase, borrowed from Lynne Sachs’ film “A Month of Single Frames,” perfectly captures the relationality that this program embodies: birth, death, motherhood, illness, widowhood, friendship, family, gender, artistry. These films, deeply anchored in the challenging realities of the everyday, are ultimately uplifting.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Explant/Implant (Josh Weisbach | color/sound | 3:16 | 16mm print | US)

A lifetime of surgeries continues with an upgrade in battery life and a downgrade in scar tissue when the filmmaker has his original pacemaker replaced after sixteen years.

Objectionable Fruit (Gabby Follett and Hogan Seidel | color/sound | 15:00 16mm to digital | US)

“Objectionable Fruit” is an experimental documentary examining the Ginkgo tree—a living fossil celebrated for its resilience and unique capacity to change sexes, defying human-imposed binaries. Using the Ginkgo as a metaphor for fluidity and endurance, the film weaves together themes of gender identity, ecological interconnectedness, and the nuanced complexities of trans existence.

Dyade (Carole Thibaud & Bertille LaFarge | b&w/sound | 6:50 | 16mm to digital | France)

A film made by two sisters, filmmaker and dancer. Written by four hands, shot and danced in turn. Witness to a shared experience, created through the inspiration of the moment, the light, and the place. A story of gesture, transmission, play, and poetry. The film images were shot in 16mm at the Bressieux farm (Savoie, France) in February 2023, developed in Mire’s shared laboratory in Nantes, and edited back and forth.

You May Laugh at Me a Little (Yuula Benivolski | color/sound | 22:35 | 16mm to digital | CA/Palestine)

A film about a glassblower in Hebron—a place historically known for glass production, which dominated the region for centuries. Each family in the business was known for their own traditional recipe. A couple of years ago I interviewed the last glassblower in Hebron’s old city, and filmed him during a regular day at his studio.

The Algae (Ursula Brookbank | b&w/sound | 5:45 | 16mm to digital | US)

Three sisters of sorrow bring tears and comfort to a widow.

Moving Feelings (Rendro Aryo | color/sound | 5:38 |Super 8 to digital l Indonesia)

An experimental poetry film shot using a super 8 mm camera from 1975. A film that plays with poetry through poetic images. A man and a woman searching and questioning the meaning of youth.

To My Son (Linda Fenstermaker | color/sound | 6:40 | 16mm to digital | US)

A visual exploration on the transition to motherhood and how time shifts in this phase of life seen through the landscapes of the Pacific Northwest.

A Month of Single Frames (Lynne Sachs | color/sound | S 8 to digital | US)

In 1998, filmmaker Barbara Hammer had a one-month artist residency in the C Scape Duneshack which is run by the Provincetown Community Compact in Cape Cod, Massachusetts. The shack had no running water or electricity. While there, she shot 16mm film with her Beaulieu camera, recorded sounds with her cassette recorder and kept a journal. In 2018, Barbara began her own process of dying by revisiting her personal archive. She gave all of her Duneshack images, sounds and writing to filmmaker Lynne Sachs and invited her to make a film with the material.

“While editing the film, the words on the screen came to me in a dream. I was really trying to figure out a way to talk to the experience of solitude that Barbara had had, how to be there with her somehow through the time that we would all share together watching her and the film. My text is a confrontation with a somatic cinema that brings us all together in multiple spaces at once.”

— Lynne Sachs

films.title: Entanglements (Shorts)
films.description:
What’s in a label? This shorts program follows attractions and relationships through change and self-discovery. Beyond the meet-cute, connecting can be complicated- let’s do it anyway!

SHORTS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Buffalo 10 (Trisha Pickelhaupt, United States, 12m)

A trans woman aching for the simplicity of her upbringing moves back to Buffalo from NYC, where she gets asked out at the local bowling alley.

Wall Udder (Alexandra Hayden, United States , 8m)

A dissatisfied woman confronts repressed feelings of malaise after her partner comes home smelling like milk.

Devils in The Bush (Juliet Belisario, Canada, 8m)

Following the disappearance of her girlfriend, a trans filmmaker discovers EmileCam, a 24-hour livestream devoted to spying on her.

La Perla Victoria, Desde un Corazón Trans (Sol Jimenez Palacios, Devyn Galindo, Victoria Castro, United States, 9m)

La Perla Victoria resists narratives that reduce trans migrants to mere victims. Instead, it offers a portrait of trans life that is tender, political, and profoundly human, rooted in the belief that telling our stories is itself a form of liberation.

CW: Descriptions of gun violence and assault, descriptions imprisonment at the US border

Saved Me (TJ Gascho, United States, 3m)

Love knows no bounds! A Seattle film screening comes to life as Cupid’s arrow flies off the screen and into the crowd!

Sword Over The Door (Alec Mazzoli, United States, 14m)

Four friends playing a tabletop roleplaying game slowly realize that something is wrong.

CW: Flashing lights, camera techniques that may affect those prone to dizziness or vertigo.

Zombie Butterflies (Pê Moreira, Thomas Argos, Brazil, 17m)

In this romcom stained with Brazilian queerness, João used to think the butterflies in his stomach were dead. When he falls in love with Lucas, his best friend, something weird starts happening in his belly. Maybe he has zombie butterflies.

Motherhood (Ava Corder, United States, 12m)

A pregnant trans woman in the heat of active labor battles strict medical protocols and her family’s doubts to have a natural birth.

CW: Blood/gore

films.title: Everything for Sale
films.description: The lead protagonist of a film disappears mid production, and his family and crew search for him before tragic news reaches them. Wajda’s first film where he received sole screenwriting credit, this deeply personal homage to his beloved actor Zbigniew Cybulski, the star of Ashes and Diamonds, is also a scathing portrait of the film industry. The film-within-a-film mirrors the real life tragedy, with actors channeling their real life experiences into their performances. Weaving together autobiography and fiction, Wajda questions what it means to be an artist and how we mourn by creating legends as a way to interpret the past.

films.title: Five Minutes to Die!
films.description:
It's FIVE MINUTES TO LIVE... HALLOWEEN EDITION!

Here's the deal. You buy a ticket. We show you the first five minutes of five different mystery movies. Then everybody votes on which one to watch in its entirety!

You've got FIVE MINUTES TO DIE! Come have an encounter with the unexpected free from the burden of preconceptions. Choose your own adventure in the unimaginably vast world of strange and interesting cinema. Experience the delight of pure surprise. We'll promise a wild time if you promise to be open to anything.

films.title: Flesh & Fluids (Shorts)
films.description:
Let’s talk about sex, maybe…let’s talk about you and ‘we’. Let’s talk about all the touching, yearning, thinking, and wanting. This shorts program is about the the flesh, and for the flesh!

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Dyson (Clac, Fara Renaud, Belgium, 14m)

Some people seek diamonds, Roxane just wants a fancy vacuum cleaner. With Trinity and Julia’s help, she is set to make her wettest dream come true.

Cockroach (Justice Maya Singleton, Liliana Padilla, United States, 22m)

A black transgender man plans to exchange sex for top surgery money with an older gay man until his night hook up turns into a hunt for a cockroach who inspires him to open his heart and conquer his fears.

Not Exactly Strangers (Ryan Rox, United States, 15m)

A tipsy hookup between a Latine trans woman and a rough-edged skater boy from her past becomes a comedic, yet intimate deep-dive into post-surgical sex, lingering history, and a body she’s still learning to celebrate.

pounded (Lis Walter, Germany, 10m)

Pounded explores what it means to be treated like a juicy piece of meat and why, for its protagonists, this does not equal objectification.

The Duties of a Lighthouse Keeper (Rory Midhani, Germany, 8m)

This film follows the daily life of an isolated seaman, all alone on a hard, hard rock, going about his duties whilst yearning for the touch of his fellow man. Is there more to this life than servicing the buoys?

Touching Ugliness (Ultra, Brazil, 15m)

With an entirely trans cast, Ugliness is a film-poetry about faith, scars and the beauty of what cannot be saved.

CW: Flashing lights, suspension play

films.title: Flying Embers and a Fortress
films.description:
PRESENTED BY TANOD LUPA & ICHRP-WA

Farmer-activist Jonas Burgos, son of the late press freedom icon and anti-Marcos publisher Jose Burgos Jr., had just finished a training program on organic farming for members of the Philippine peasant organization Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP), when he was abducted on April 28, 2007. The abduction was brazen—carried out at noon in a crowded mall. As his family launched their search, a car plate brought them face-to-face with powerful forces. Thus began their fight for justice.

Despite insurmountable barriers, anonymous informants have provided leads and even the last known photo of Jonas in captivity. At the forefront of this battle is Edita, his 80-year-old mother, and her other son, filmmaker JL Burgos.

Presented through testimonials from their lawyer, a reporter, a former Justice Secretary and Human Rights Commission Chair, and witnesses who agreed to appear on condition of anonymity, combined with animation and never-before-seen footage of the family’s relentless search, JL pieces the stories together to uncover the painful truths about his brother’s disappearance.

This 2024 documentary is a timely examination of the rights abuses that activists and organizers continue to face today in the Philippines under the Marcos Jr. administration, especially as KMP still carries out a national day of action in the Philippines for landless farmers annually on October 21st. Join Tanod Lupa at the Beacon for these screenings and discussion on how this relates to our current community, as we carry out demands of Justice for the Negros 19 massacre and justice for the rights and welfare of peasant farmers throughout the Philippines.

Tanod Lupa (Tagalog for “Earth Guardian”) is an organization based in South Seattle building solidarity with land defenders as they struggle against environmental destruction and degradation. TL is a member of the Friends of the Filipino People in Struggle (FFPS) network and the International Coalition for Human Rights in the Philippines (ICHRP).

films.title: Food of the Gods Part II
films.description:
Neil Hamilton (Paul Coufos, CHOPPING MALL) is a brilliant scientist on the verge of a breakthrough with a growth hormone that could enlarge food supply and end world hunger. However, when the test subjects - a group of lab rats - escape, they begin to wreak havoc all across the streets of Mississauga, Ontario New York City! Directed by Damian Lee (MST3K favorite ABRAXAS, GUARDIAN OF THE UNIVERSE), co-written by Mike Werb (THE MASK, FACE/OFF), and co-starring Lisa Schrage (HELLO MARY LOU: PROM NIGHT 2), FOOD OF THE GODS PART 2 - alternately titled GNAW - is a name-only sequel to the 1976 adaptation of the H.G. Wells novel that is relentless in its gruesomeness and bafflingly entertaining in its storytelling in equal measure. Not to mention a scene that is so jaw-dropping that it has become an out-of-context meme for years (you’ll know it when you see it). Analog Anomalies is proud to bring you this gore-fest the way it was meant to be seen: on glorious VHS!

FOOD OF THE GODS PART 2 is presented as part of Analog Anomalies, a monthly series that features the weirdest and wildest genre films that are not available for rent, purchase, or streaming on a digital platform.

films.title: Forgotten Island
films.description:
While celebrating their last night together, Jo and Raissa stumble upon a mysterious portal that transports them to the fantastical island of Nakali, packed with magical and mythological creatures they grew up hearing stories about from their Filipino families.

Some of these figures will become friends, some foes. Joined by well-meaning-but- hapless weredog Raww (Dave Franco) and a small-but-mighty pack of pals, Jo and Raissa must face The Dreaded Manananggal (Tony winning icon Lea Salonga), the most feared creature on the island. When they discover that the memories of their entire friendship are the price for returning home, Jo and Raissa will race to find a way to leave the island before they forget each other forever.

films.title: Frankenstein
films.description:
The classic Universal horror hit attacks the screen at Central Cinema.

Dr. Henry Frankenstein obsesses over creating life. He's so obsessed that he assembles a creature from body parts of the dead. He and his assistant Fritz then bring the being to life; great success! Except, oops, the creature escapes and wreaks havoc (both accidentally and on purpose) on the nearby countryside.

Based on Mary Shelly's sci-fi horror classic, Universal took the creature from her book and made him an icon. Boris Karloff's work as the creature holds up as one of horror's most remembered performances. Director James Whale delivers an audience pleasing tale that doesn't shy from the moral questions the book raises

films.title: Fright Night
films.description:
Meet Jerry Dandrige. He's sweet, handsome, and likes to sleep in late. You might think he's the perfect neighbor. But before inviting Jerry in for a nightcap, there's one thing you should know: Jerry's drink of choice is warm, red, and straight from the jugular!

Only 17-year-old Charley Brewster knows his neighbor's bloodcurdling secret. When Charley can't get anyone to believe him, he turns to TV horror host Peter Vincent who at one point was the "Great Vampire Killer of the movies. But Jerry gets wise to the duo's intentions, and sets his sights on those Charley holds dearest.

Fright Night is a beloved 80's horror comedy for good reason, with as many laughs as frights on screen making for a fun flick to see on an October night.

films.title: Ghost Squad
films.description: Three unpopular friends accept a dare to spend Halloween in a haunted house. They encounter a mischievous ghost dog intent on tormenting them, leading to a night of terrifying chaos as they struggle to survive the supernatural encounter

films.title: Ginger Snaps
films.description: Directed by John Fawcett and cowritten by Karen Walton, Ginger Snaps, a cult classic from Canada, is a supernatural coming-of-age story centering around two misfit sisters, 15-year-old Brigitte Fitzgerald and almost 16-year-old Ginger, who are obsessed with dying and bound by a childhood pact to stay together forever. Their loathing of mind-numbing suburban existence quickly changes to a survival-first mindset when Ginger is savagely attacked by a werewolf while walking at night in the woods. She survives and her external wounds heal, but something is clearly not the same. Ginger Snaps cleverly turns Ginger’s monthly werewolf cravings into a transgressive metaphor about the strange and mysterious horror of becoming a woman. — MoMA

films.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
films.description:
War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life.

Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant.

There is no third time. Everything ends here.

films.title: Green Room
films.description:
Green Room is a brilliantly crafted and wickedly fun horror-thriller starring Patrick Stewart as a diabolical club owner who squares off against an unsuspecting but resilient young punk band.

Down on their luck punk rockers The Ain’t Rights are finishing up a long and unsuccessful tour, and are about to call it quits when they get an unexpected booking at an isolated, run-down club deep in the backwoods of Oregon. What seems merely to be a third-rate gig escalates into something much more sinister when they witness an act of violence backstage that they weren’t meant to see. Now trapped backstage, they must face off against the club’s depraved owner, Darcy Banker (Stewart), a man who will do anything to protect the secrets of his nefarious enterprise. But while Darcy and his henchmen think the band will be easy to get rid of, The Ain’t Rights prove themselves much more cunning and capable than anyone expected, turning the tables on their unsuspecting captors and setting the stage for the ultimate life-or-death showdown.

films.title: Grosse Pointe Blank
films.description:
After assassin Martin Blank has trouble focusing on his work, reulting in a failed assignment, he returns to his homestown of Grosse Point, Michigan, for his 10-year high school reunion. There he reconnects with Debi, his ex-girlfriend whom he jilted on prom night. Meanwhile, work gets in the way of his personal time when a Grosse Point local becomes a possible target, and a rival hitman rolls into town.

Smart, funny, and sporting a fantastic soundtrack, Grosse Point Blank is among John Cusack's finest comedies and a great example oh how to make an upbeat rom-com with a twisted sense of humor.

films.title: Halloween III
films.description:
It's time for the Baron's annual screening of what is perhaps the weirdest wildest sequels 80's horror has to offer.

When a novelty-toy salesman is attacked by a deadly crew of men in suits, his doctor and his daughter hit the road to uncover a plot that goes massively over the top. Honestly, this film is never under the top. Only over. Just when you think no more weird things can happen...well, you get the idea.

This is the rogue 1982 sequel that does its own thing. Thankfully, Baron Von Terror will be there to unpack our journey together, and trust us, there is a LOT to unpack.

films.title: HAUNTED DESTINATION New film from local filmmaker Taylor Guterson
films.description:
The new film from local filmmaker Taylor Guterson screens one night only at the North Bend Theatre for free!

When strange stories and unexplained incidents begin piling up around North Bend, the town sees an opportunity to reinvent itself as a haunted destination, launching a publicity stunt designed to put the little mountain town on the map. The mayor embraces the idea, while the sheriff remains convinced it is a terrible idea. To help sell the story, the city brings in a team of paranormal investigators to document the town's supposed activity, but what begins as a promotional stunt takes an unsettling turn when one of the investigators disappears. As the mystery unfolds, the story reaches back to Moncton, the settlement that once stood where the waters of Rattlesnake Lake are today, and the people who lost their homes, their community, and their lives when the town was flooded as part of Seattle's effort to secure its water supply. Years later, a young girl becomes fascinated by the legend and, for a school project, travels with her father to Seattle to meet one of the surviving investigators and uncover what really happened

films.title: Hausu (House)
films.description:
The Japanese fantasy horror is an annual must see at Central Cinema.
Come visit the house with your friends Gorgeous, Prof, Fantasy, Melody, and Kung Fu. Just don't touch the piano without permission.

films.title: Heart of the Beast
films.description: After a harrowing plane crash, Special Forces officer James Belmont and his combat dog, Odin, find themselves stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness. Together, they are forced into a brutal fight for survival against the elements.
