films.title: Hocus Pocus
films.description: In this bewitching story, three mischievous witches are inadvertently resurrected when teenager Max Dennison discovers an ancient spellbook in Salem. Along with his sister Dani and new friend Allison, Max must stop the witches from carrying out a nefarious plan. The trio of witches, portrayed by Bette Midler, Sarah Jessica Parker, and Kathy Najimy, wreak havoc as the children race to steal their spellbook and prevent a wicked curse from engulfing the town

films.title: Holy Trinity
films.description:
After an incident huffing her drug of choice—a mysterious aerosol can from the ubiquitous Glamhag brand—Trinity finds herself with a newfound gift for speaking to the dead. Confused and more than a little curious about this strange turn of events, she seeks the counsel of a colorful cast of characters, from priests and drag queens to a witch and more, all of whom teach her their unique spiritual practices.

As she navigates life with this unexpected talent (and continues to huff that mysterious drug), Trinity is tossed between hallucination and reality more and more frequently, developing a growing confidence in her strange new ability and learning to harness it in surprising ways. But with any great power comes great responsibility, and soon Trinity has to decide what’s more important: her community and personal relationships or the allure of influence and fame

Boasting an inclusive cast (including Theo Germaine from Netflix’s The Politician) and crew comprised of diverse communities often neglected in mainstream cinema and approaching typically taboo subjects with verve and acceptance, Holy Trinity is a sometimes raunchy, always entertaining celebration of all that makes us different. In their feature film debut, writer, director and star Glamhag presents a vibrant and vivid portrait of friendship, spirituality and community, with more than a little glam sprinkled in along the way.

films.title: I Walked with a Zombie
films.description:
Among the extraordinary cycle of horror films produced by Val Lewton at RKO, I WALKED WITH A ZOMBIE may be the most dreamlike and beautiful. Taking a sensational title imposed by the studio and a story loosely modeled on Jane Eyre, Lewton and director Jacques Tourneur fashioned an entrancing journey into the realm between life and death, where romantic obsession and supernatural mystery are inseparable from the lingering wounds of colonial history.

Frances Dee stars as a young Canadian nurse who travels to the Caribbean island of Saint Sebastian to care for the mysteriously unresponsive wife of a wealthy plantation owner. Her search for a cure draws her deeper into the island and toward a world of Vodou ritual, family secrets, and the possibility that her patient may be neither entirely alive nor entirely dead. Lewton and Tourneur treat that mystery with remarkable seriousness, finding their horror not in conventional shocks but in suggestion, sound, and images of almost supernatural beauty.

Sugarcane sways in a moonlit field. Drums echo through the darkness. The towering figure of Carrefour stands silently at a crossroads. Few Hollywood horror films have ever made nighttime feel so mysterious or so alive. Haunting, melancholy, and hypnotic, I WALKED WITH A ZOMBIE transforms its unlikely combination of Gothic romance and zombie mythology into something closer to a waking dream—one of the strangest and most beautiful achievements of studio-era horror.

films.title: Idle Hands
films.description:
Anton is a teenage burnout whose daily agenda consists of smoking weed, watching TV and accomplishing absolutely nothing. Then his right hand gets possessed by the devil and murders his parents. Soon his two best friends are dead, Anton is trying to cut off his own arm, and the hottest girl in the neighborhood is somehow still interested in him. Luckily, death doesn’t prevent anybody from hanging out.

IDLE HANDS could only have escaped from 1999: Devon Sawa in enormous pants, Seth Green and Elden Henson as undead couch potatoes, Jessica Alba in angel wings, The Offspring playing the school Halloween dance and Rob Zombie’s “Dragula” on MTV while everybody gets high on the couch. It captures teenage life in the last few minutes before everything went digital—a suburban wasteland of weed, music videos, convenience stores and endless hours with absolutely nothing to do. Then it dumps a homicidal severed hand into the middle of it and starts spraying glorious rubber gore. Some of it has aged badly, some of it has aged beautifully, and somehow this deeply stupid movie has only grown more lovable with tim

films.title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
films.description: Strange pods have arrived from outer space unnoticed, and suddenly the people of San Francisco are beginning to act very, very differently. With Elizabeth (Brooke Adams), Jack (Jeff Goldblum), and psychiatrist Dr. David Kibner (Leonard Nimoy) by his side, Bennell follows a trail of increasingly bizarre clues into a nightmare where nobody—not even those closest to you—can be trusted. Kaufman slowly turns the familiar streets of San Francisco into a paranoid fever dream, filling each frame with a mounting sense of dread as the city plunges into fear and mistrust. Paired with Michael Chapman’s (Raging Bull) gritty cinematography and the film’s astonishing special effects, every encounter becomes potentially sinister. More than a sci-fi horror thriller, Invasion of the Body Snatchers is a terrifying vision of urban alienation and the loss of individuality—and its final image may be one of the most horrifying in movie history. Remember: if you notice an eerie change in someone close to you, chances are you’re next! Sleep tight.

films.title: Irreversible
films.description:
One night. An unforgivable act. A tale told in reverse.

Acclaimed filmmaker Gaspar Noé’s unflinching exploration of human savagery and the uncompromising nature of time, Irreversible was met with a groundswell of acclaim and uproar upon its premiere at Cannes in 2002. Stylish, sexually frank, and brutal, the film’s conceit of exploring the events of one terrible night on the streets of Paris in reverse chronological order was celebrated and derided in equal measure, helping to further cement Noé’s legacy as a cinematic enfant terrible.

films.title: Isle of the Dead
films.description:
War, plague, superstition, premature burial and Boris Karloff, all trapped together on a tiny Greek island. Inspired by Arnold Böcklin’s famously ominous painting, ISLE OF THE DEAD finds producer Val Lewton at his most morbid, surrounding a handful of characters with death and slowly closing off every possible escape.

During the Balkan Wars of 1912, Karloff’s severe General Pherides travels to an island cemetery to visit his wife’s grave, only to discover that plague has arrived before him. The island is placed under quarantine, and as its inhabitants begin dying one by one, an elderly woman insists that disease isn’t the only thing preying upon them. She suspects a vorvolaka, a vampiric creature of Greek folklore. Pherides initially dismisses such beliefs as dangerous superstition, but as the deaths mount and isolation takes its toll, his certainty begins to crumble. Karloff gives one of his richest performances as a man accustomed to commanding soldiers who discovers that neither discipline nor reason can command death.

Lewton and director Mark Robson turn the island into a suffocating chamber of graves, shuttered rooms and mounting fear, where plague and superstition seem to spread together. Patient and dread-filled, ISLE OF THE DEAD saves its most terrible visions for the final stretch, when its restrained study of people under pressure gives way to one of the great nightmares of 1940s horror. Even James Agee, otherwise skeptical of the film, called its final half hour “as brutally frightening and gratifying a horror movie as I can remember.” Few films in Lewton’s extraordinary RKO cycle stare more directly into the grave.

films.title: Jennifer's Body
films.description: Megan Fox stars in this horror-comedy about a high school cheerleader who develops an insatiable appetite for her male classmates after she’s possessed by a hungry demon.

films.title: Joybubbles
films.description:
In the 1950s, a boy discovers he can control the global telephone system simply by whistling a magic tone. Born blind and hungry for connection, his early obsession with the telephone sparks a subculture that shapes the future of hacking and modern technology in the 20th century.

Told through vivid archival footage and Joybubbles’ own voice recordings, the film celebrates a visionary who redefined connection and challenged assumptions about disability, identity, and imagination.

Joybubbles pulses with the curiosity and wonder he brought to the world, brought to life through director Rachael J. Morrison’s inventive, tactile storytelling.

Presented with open audio description and open captions

films.title: Jucks
films.description:
Set in Denver City, 2064 AD, JUCKS is an experimental sci-fi silent film. It follows a haunted protagonist who enters a dystopian landscape lorded by an omniscient radio frequency known as Jucks, and saturated with a hallucinogenic substance. Jules searches for one thing: Gold.

CW: Flashing lights, blood/gore

SCREENS WITH:

If I'm Here It Is By Mystery (Clari Ribeiro, Brazil, 20m)

New Rio, 2054. Renowned witch Dahlia arrives at the port with a mission: to found the most powerful Clan that has ever existed and thus defeat the Order of Truth. In the future, many people are trans — but only a few are witches.

CW: Stabbing of a trans woman, blood/gore

films.title: Kanał
films.description: In the final stages of the 1944 Warsaw Uprising, a unit of Polish Home Army resistance fighters attempt to escape the Nazi aggressors through a hellish descent through the labyrinthian city sewers. Jerzy Lipman's claustrophobic, high contrast cinematography conveys their nightmarish struggle along the road to freedom. Based on true events, the film brought Wajda international acclaim for its evocative portrait of strength, duty and hope in the face of insurmountable odds.

films.title: L’Amour Fou
films.description:
Confined to decades of oblivion after its original celluloid elements were damaged in a fire, Jacques Rivette’s formally brilliant and psychologically lacerating L’AMOUR FOU — among the most important and legendary films of the French New Wave — has been meticulously restored and will be presented by critic A.S. Hamrah in celebration of his recent collection ALGORITHM OF THE NIGHT!

Arguably the most extreme, radical, and essential of the French auteur’s films, L’AMOUR FOU was Rivette’s first feature to introduce the signature characteristics of his visionary cinema, including a durational gamesmanship and reflexive interplays between film, theatre, art, and life.

Narcissistic theatre director Sebastian (Jean-Pierre Kalfon) is staging and rehearsing a minimalist adaptation of Racine’s Andromaque while an independent television crew (led by André Labarthe) shoots a documentary of the preparations in real time, their handheld 16mm footage cut alongside the rest of the film shot on 35mm. Under extreme pressure, Sebastian’s actor wife Claire (Bulle Ogier, never more luminous) buckles and anxiously abandons her role, only to be replaced by his ex, further spurring her jealousy, isolation, and paranoia.

A portrait of mad love and of unbridled and boundless passion that threatens to eclipse (even annihilate) the self, over four hypnotic, spellbinding hours, L’AMOUR FOU weds astonishing improvisation with raw psychodrama, defying the limits of reality as life and art risk dangerously, desirously subsuming one another.

films.title: La bola negra
films.description: La bola negra, also known as The Black Ball, inspired by an unfinished play by Federico García Lorca, will be a queer vindication about three men in three different moments of Spanish history: 1932, 1937, and 2017.

films.title: Lady
films.description:
“Those of us pining for Sian Clifford since the end of 'Fleabag' . . . have been rewarded with an outrageous barnstormer in this bizarre mockumentary comedy.” – Peter Bradshaw, The Guardian

In pursuit of his first big break (and, more importantly, the promise of a Netflix deal), young documentarian Sam agrees to meet with the aristocratic Lady Isabella at her imposing country estate, Ravenhyde Hall. However, even he is shocked by the immense scope of her patrician pompousness and eccentric behavior. Obscenely self-absorbed, she describes herself as "the aristocracy's answer to the Kardashians". Her envisioned vanity project, for which she wants Sam to film the making-of, entails an ill-conceived multimedia performance art showcase to debut at the Stately Stars, a local talent show competition for youth held annually at the Hall. Sam agrees to her proposition, sensing a ripe opportunity to skewer Lady Isabella's artistic pretensions, presenting her creative endeavor as nothing more than privileged self-entitlement. And then something unseen and quite strange begins to happen. Sian Clifford, who played Phoebe Waller-Bridge's sister in "Fleabag", gives a riotously unhinged performance as Lady Isabella, while director Sam Abrahams brilliantly utilizes the mockumentary format to fashion a comic narrative that plays out like an unholy communion of Grey Gardens, Sunset Boulevard, and "Ab Fab" at its most absurd.

films.title: Land of the Dead: it's for the gays
films.description: Presented by Scorpio Rising Productions. Land of the Dead: it’s for the gays is a dark, campy horror comedy that explores the intersections of gender identity, addiction, trauma, and Queerness. Through Mel’s confrontation with a literal demon from their past, the film examines the ways unresolved pain can shape identity, relationships, and self-acceptance. Blending supernatural horror with Queer humor and emotional depth, the story uses camp as a tool for both survival and reclamation, creating a space where confronting the past becomes a path toward healing and embracing one’s authentic self.

films.title: Landscape in the Mist
films.description:
Voula and her younger brother Alexandros leave home in search of the father they have never met, whom they believe is waiting for them somewhere in Germany. Certain only that they must keep going, the two children set out across a cold, wintry Greece by train, on foot and in the cars of strangers. From this simple journey, Theo Angelopoulos creates one of the most beautiful and emotionally overwhelming films of the 1980s.

LANDSCAPE IN THE MIST moves at the pace of discovery. Angelopoulos allows his long takes to unfold until places that initially seem ordinary acquire a strange and monumental power. Giorgos Arvanitis’ extraordinary cinematography makes the children appear very small within landscapes whose scale and meanings they are only beginning to understand, while Eleni Karaindrou’s aching score opens another emotional dimension within the images. Again and again, Angelopoulos gives us time to look until what we are looking at has somehow changed.

Their journey brings encounters with strangers, fleeting friendships, moments of tenderness and danger, and sudden visions of astonishing beauty. Angelopoulos never hurries toward them. He lets weather gather, silence deepen, figures cross enormous distances and moments unfold until reality slips almost imperceptibly into something mysterious and sublime. Haunting, deeply moving and filled with images that remain lodged in the memory, LANDSCAPE IN THE MIST is slow cinema at its most emotionally immediate: two children moving urgently through a world much larger, older, crueler and more beautiful than they yet know.

films.title: Le Bonheur (Happiness)
films.description: A film-funding opportunity arose, but Agnès Varda would have to write fast. A darkly comic idea about marriage had been “lurking” inside her, and it came gushing out. She summed up the film as “a ripe summer peach with a worm inside,” and began filming. François, a village carpenter (Jean-Claude Drouot), his dressmaker wife Thérèse (Claire Druout) and their darling daughter and son, stroll through an Impressionist landscape of yellow sunflowers, bright evergreens, blue and red blossoms, and picnic on the grass. All is harmony and bliss. Varda believes we discover who we are through encounters with others, not through solitary soul-searching: “encounters make us less unhappy.” Contented family man François feels an added air of euphoria when he encounters the young, modern, single Émilie (Marie-France Boyer), who works at the post office. He’s no seducer, his loving feeling of happiness simply expands to include Boyer, and he wants to share it with those dearest to him. Romantics, feminists, traditionalists and free-thinkers have debated this gorgeous, provocative film for decades.

films.title: Lost Boys
films.description: Following their parents' divorce, Micheal and his younger brother Sam relocate to the trendy beach town of Santa Carla, California with their mother. Moving in with Lucy's eccentric father, they quickly discover that Santa Carla, often referred to as the murder capital of the world, is home to a lively boardwalk frequented by a group of intriguing young men led by the enigmatic David.

films.title: Mad Monster Party?
films.description:
By 1967, the monsters had made it. Dracula, Frankenstein, the Wolf Man and the rest of the old horror gang had escaped the graveyard and taken over television, toy stores, model kits, comic books and the bedrooms of monster-crazed kids everywhere. There was really only one thing left to do: throw a party.

And what a party. Rankin/Bass took the stop-motion wizardry behind RUDOLPH THE RED-NOSED REINDEER, handed the monsters over to MAD Magazine legends Harvey Kurtzman and Jack Davis, brought in Boris Karloff to preside over the festivities and Phyllis Diller to play Frankenstein’s extremely talkative mate, then invited every creature they could squeeze onto the Isle of Evil. Dracula! The Wolf Man! The Mummy! Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde! The Invisible Man! Zombies! Skeletons! A Peter Lorre-looking ghoul! Jack Davis designed them, a studio full of Japanese animators built them, and somebody had to move every single one of these maniacs one frame at a time.

The result is a glorious 1960s monster-kid fever dream where Frankenstein discovers a formula capable of destroying all matter and celebrates by announcing his retirement. There are musical numbers, terrible puns, monster politics, a skeleton rock band called Little Tibia and the Fibias, Dracula dancing and enough lovingly handcrafted gothic clutter to fill a dozen Halloween specials. Part monster rally, part MAD Magazine cartoon brought to life and part Rankin/Bass holiday special for the greatest holiday of them all, MAD MONSTER PARTY? is what happens when an entire generation stops being afraid of monsters and starts letting them babysit their kids.

films.title: Making Marie Antoinette
films.description:
Eleanor Coppola's behind-the-scenes documentation of her daughter Sofia directing the 2006 film MARIE ANTOINETTE, capturing the craftsmanship and challenges of being a young female director.

Polarizing upon its release, Sofia Coppola’s MARIE ANTOINETTE is now, 20 years later, widely embraced as a 21st-century cinematic cornerstone and a distilled expression of its director’s recurring themes of celebrity, wealth, and isolation. For the first time, Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating her personal vision for the brief life of the 18th-century queen in the years leading up to the French Revolution is on full display in this diary shot by her mother, filmmaker Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005.

From almost 80 hours of video, Eleanor began to assemble the footage during the pandemic lockdown, and Sofia helped finish editing it after Eleanor’s death in 2024. Narrated by Diane Lane, reciting Eleanor’s journals from the time, this is a rare behind-the-scenes glimpse that is both process-oriented and touchingly personal.

films.title: Man of Marble
films.description: In the 1970s, student filmmaker Agnieszka investigates the life of a 1950s bricklayer and discredited labor hero who is only remembered through statue representations in cellars and storage lockers. Discovering facts about the bricklayer have been suppressed, she has to decide whether to pursue the truth or not while navigating the complexities of communism's rise in Poland. Mixing satirical humor and poetic storytelling, this thought-provoking examination of the moral responsibility of an individual and the way art can challenge dominant ideology remains one of Wajda’s most unique productions.

films.title: Marie Antoinette
films.description:
20th anniversary screening of Sofia Coppola's pastel-soaked cult classic, newly restored in 4K.

Coppola brings a candy-colored palette, a dreamy synth-pop soundtrack, and Converse high-tops to eighteenth-century Versailles for this exuberantly subversive, extravagantly stylized anti-biopic of one of history’s most infamous (and perhaps misunderstood) figures.

Kirsten Dunst portrays Marie Antoinette as a rebellious teenage princess, who marries the awkward young dauphin of France (Jason Schwartzman), soon to be crowned King Louis XVI. Feeling isolated in a royal court rife with scandal and intrigue, Marie Antoinette defies both royalty and commoner by living like a rock star—which can work for only so long.

Named the 10th best movie of the 21st century by The Big Picture podcast.

films.title: Members Only Mystery Preview - November 2026
films.description: Have you ever wanted to get a sneak preview of some of The Forum’s upcoming programming at an exclusive, members-only event? This is your chance to do just that! Join us for our November 2026 installment of our Members Only Mystery Screenings, where we can promise you you’ll be treated to an evening with a fantastic film, but you’ll only know what it is right before you see it!

films.title: Met Opera 2026/2027: Macbeth
films.description: Two of opera’s most extraordinary artists return to The Met: Live in HD for Verdi’s thrilling take on the immortal Shakespearean tale of the scheming couple determined to seize power at any cost. Baritone Quinn Kelsey is the Scottish king haunted by the ghosts of his murderous ascent to the throne, opposite soprano Lise Davidsen as the power-mad Lady Macbeth, whose ruinous ambition damns them both. Met Music Director Yannick Nézet-Séguin takes the podium for a penetrating production by Louisa Proske. Rounding out the all-star cast are tenor Freddie De Tommaso as Macduff and bass-baritone Ryan Speedo Green as Banquo.

films.title: Mutable Archive (Shorts)
films.description:
How does time alter how we interact with our personal records and artifacts? How can we create friction within memory, photographs, and videos? A palpable collection of stories that intertwine the past, present, and self, on the way into the unknown.

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

In Another Life (Tristan Blue, United States, 9m)

An elder queer hermit searches through coastal soundscapes in pursuit of a mysterious cave they believe will allow them to commune with a past self.

CW: Flashing lights

My 50 Minute Breath-Hold Speedrun Challenge (Emery Joan, United States, 2m)

“I try to hold my breath for 50 minutes in real time as quickly as I can.”

giiwe πρό bizhiw / bizhiw πρό giiwe (mystery byrd, Canada, 3m)

“A home video, dedicated to my baby.”

b.longing (mystery byrd, Canada, 7m)

A dialogue and poetic home video about belonging, from young people living in modern capitalist colonial society.

Somewhere within me (Andoeni Padilla, Mexico, 18m)

A story of a friendship told through childhood archival material. They try to answer who they are, who they wish to be, and inevitably, they turn to who they have been.

Unhappy Sexy Girl (Cassidy Civiero, Canada, 7m)

A transmasc filmmaker revisits his past as an unhappy sexy girl coping through constant marijuana and sexual objectification.

Vollúpya (Éri Sarmet, Jocimar Dias Jr., Brazil, 20m)

In a post-apocalyptic future, an intergalactic explorer lands at an abandoned museum on a quest to find traces of his long-lost ancestors, and ends up being teleported to the dance floor of a Brazilian queer nightclub in the 1990s.

CW: Flashing lights

films.title: Nagarkirtan
films.description: Parimal is a woman trapped in a man’s body who runs away from home and joins a ghetto of eunuchs as Puti and sings at traffic signals to earn money. There she falls in love with Madhu, a delivery boy with a Chinese restaurant who moonlights as a flautist in kirtans. The love blossoms even as Puti dreams of raising the money required for the sex reassignment surgery.

films.title: Naza
films.description:
Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza. The film's title - NAZA - is a term that appears throughout the documentary. It is a military acronym euphemistically used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that it expects will be killed in an airstrike.

Directors' Note
We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

— Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

films.title: Necropolis
films.description:
Frankenstein’s monster, Countess Bathory, Attila the Hun, Montezuma, the Devil, witches and other ghosts of history and literature drift through Franco Brocani’s extraordinary NECROPOLIS, a plotless procession of tableaux, monologues and mysterious rituals set somewhere between a ruined civilization and the creative subconscious.

Characters emerge from darkness, deliver delirious confessions and disappear again into a psychedelic labyrinth of bare stages, Pop Art debris and shifting identities. Warhol superstar Viva becomes Bathory, Carmelo Bene plays the Devil, Tina Aumont appears as a witch, and Pierre Clémenti rides naked through the void on a white horse as Attila the Hun, while conversations wander through sex and revolution, religion and magic, madness and death to Gavin Bryars’ hypnotic minimalist score.

Nothing like a conventional horror film but not playing by the rules of any underground cinema either, NECROPOLIS is a strange collision of European avant-garde, theater, performance art and late-’60s counterculture—a lysergic pageant of the monsters, myths and bad dreams left behind by Western civilization.

“I cannot believe I just watched a gorgeous, enigmatic, glacially-paced arthouse film in which Frankenstein’s monster listens to the MC5 while wearing a green velvet suit. How did Franco Brocani know 50 years ago that such a thing was exactly what I needed tonight? Movies are fucking magic.” - Ipsissimu Mocata

films.title: Next of Kin
films.description:
When Linda inherits her mother’s sprawling retirement home in rural Australia, she returns to a place she hasn’t seen since childhood and discovers that the elderly residents have started dying with suspicious regularity. Then she finds her mother’s old diaries, which describe eerily similar deaths decades earlier. There are figures at windows, faucets that won’t stop running, footsteps in empty rooms and an enormous old house that seems determined to keep Linda from ever getting a decent night’s sleep.

NEXT OF KIN spends its first hour moving at the speed of a nightmare you can’t quite wake up from, then suddenly remembers it’s an Australian horror movie and all hell breaks loose. Director Tony Williams smothers the film in rain, shadows, long hallways and creeping dread, while Tangerine Dream veteran Klaus Schulze’s pulsing electronic score keeps the dread humming. Together they turn a retirement home into one of the great haunted spaces of ’80s horror without ever settling comfortably into a ghost story. Elegant, eccentric and quietly menacing, NEXT OF KIN keeps tightening the screws until its stately Gothic nightmare finally cracks open and something much wilder comes spilling out.

films.title: Night of the Living Dead
films.description: The dead come back to life and eat the living. Several people barricade themselves inside a rural house in an attempt to survive the night. Outside are hordes of relentless, shambling zombies who can only be killed by a blow to the head.

films.title: Night of the Vamp-Friars
films.description:
The first feature film wholly produced by Vinegar Syndrome Pictures; directed by Kurtis M. Spieler (Re-Director of New York Ninja).

A group of friends in a punk rock band discover a hidden cemetery in the woods, where they accidentally raise a horde of undead friars.

Shot entirely on 16mm film, Night of the Vamp-Friars is a loving tribute to the homegrown horror films made during the height of the video store era.

Presented with The Grand Illusion.

films.title: No Country for Mothers
films.description:
No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the “girl boss” and “trad wife” labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. Following activist Reshma Saujani, the film charts a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win the kind of historic support families actually need.

Join us for this family-friendly screening and community event with an age appropriate Q&A, games and activities for kids, and free Molly Moon's Homemade Ice Cream. This isn't just about watching a film; it's about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we've been carrying quietly, and realize we are not alone. We would love for you to join us.

films.title: Once Upon a Time In Seattle
films.description:
A perpetually living project, Once Upon a Time in Seattle returns to Northwest Film Forum in a revised, expanded (and shorter!?) edit for this special encore engagement. Comprised of moments from 50 films shot in Seattle (up from 47 in the previous iteration,) and a few irresistible facsimiles, Once Upon a Time in Seattle is part love letter, part loony action adventure, and part free-associative meditation on the transience of landscape in a city that has always had a complicated relationship with honoring its past while moving swiftly (recklessly?) into the future.

There is no linear narrative, and dialogue is kept to a minimum. The city itself is both location and protagonist, while the function of the human characters, or perhaps more accurately, ciphers, is that of a vessel to move us through the city and occasionally offer loose context or comic relief.

No single existing shot or sequence is sustained longer than a minute, with most individual shots lasting less than 20 seconds, and over half clocking in at 5 seconds or less. The result is a deceptively complex amalgamation of wholly unrelated material, and an impressively unique editorial/directorial achievement.

Surprisingly weaving numerous throughlines from the many disparate existing narratives, while leaving much open to the viewer’s interpretation, scene chronology floats between seemingly non sequitur, to quietly poignant, depending on the viewer’s own history with the city.

A hyper-local, one-of-a-kind film experience and an opportunity to examine Seattle’s ever-changing landscape as seen through the camera lens, Once Upon a Time in Seattle offers a unique portal to examine our city’s topography (and vibe!) of the past, both near and distant.

If you saw the premiere in September and loved it, come see how it’s changed!

films.title: Pierrot le Fou
films.description: A poet experiences the world and expresses it in words, images, emotions. Pierrot is Jean-Luc Godard’s free-form ode to “an artist and his girl in love, the last romantic couple,” made poignant because his seven-film relationship with Anna Karina, and their marriage, would soon be over. In the film they are personified as Ferdinand (Jean-Paul Belmondo) and Marianne (Anna Karina). Ferdinand, fed up with his life of oppressive bourgeois conformity, leaves his marriage-with-child for spontaneous road adventures with babysitter Marianne. In a euphoric rule-breaking rush, the couple speeds to an idyllic secluded island on the French Riviera. Ferdinand is now free to contemplate quietly and work on his book, with Marianne as his affectionate, inspiring companion. But she loves to sing and dance: “I’ve had it with nature, eating from cans, that’s it!” So its back to “civilization,” and what Marianne calls “a police novel, revolvers, nightclubs.” Ferdinand discovers that there’s more to Marianne’s story than he realized, and he responds accordingly, moment-to-moment: existential choice made profoundly literal. As Godard says, “The world between two flickers of the eyelids, the sadness between two heart-beats.” When Karina boldly gazes into Godard’s camera, at us, we feel both their hearts beating. In Godard’s deeply personal cinema, love can be both lost and eternal, the horizon where sun unites with sea.

films.title: Poltergeist
films.description:
Strange and creepy happenings beset an average California family, the Freelings -- Steve (Craig T. Nelson), Diane (JoBeth Williams), teenaged Dana (Dominique Dunne), eight-year-old Robbie (Oliver Robins), and five-year-old Carol Ann (Heather O'Rourke) -- when ghosts commune with them through the television set. Initially friendly and playful, the spirits turn unexpectedly menacing, and, when Carol Ann goes missing, Steve and Diane turn to a parapsychologist and eventually an exorcist for help.

Part of the Essential Cinema Series, bringing you films that must be seen on the big screen.

films.title: Practical Magic 2
films.description: The Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all.

films.title: Primetime
films.description: In 2006, "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

films.title: Real Steel
films.description: Charlie Kenton is a washed-up fighter who retired from the ring when robots took over the sport. After his robot is trashed, he reluctantly teams up with his estranged son to rebuild and train an unlikely contender.

films.title: Resident Evil
films.description: From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling - and terrifying - reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

films.title: Rider of the Skulls
films.description:
RIDER OF THE SKULLS has 79 minutes and refuses to waste any of them. A werewolf! A vampire! A witch! Walking skeletons! The Headless Horseman! A corpse resurrected from its coffin to identify its own murderer! Alfredo Salazar’s glorious 1965 horror-western plays like an entire Saturday matinee serial crammed into a single feature, tearing through three supernatural adventures with barely enough time between monsters to reload.

Holding this magnificent pile-up together is a masked charro dressed in black, decorated with skulls and apparently prepared to confront any supernatural menace in Mexico with the same basic equipment he’d use against cattle rustlers. The werewolf transforms from man to skeleton to wolf. The vampire turns into a wonderfully handmade flying bat. A cemetery witch summons the dead. The Headless Horseman brings skeleton henchmen. When bullets don’t work, our hero’s next strategy is generally to keep shooting, start punching or find something with a blade. Nobody questions any of this. Why would they?

Part western, part monster movie, part masked-avenger serial, RIDER OF THE SKULLS has the handmade creatures, foggy graveyards and irresistible comic-book logic of a movie dreamed up without anyone around to say no. It has very little money, three monsters to fight and absolutely no time for restraint.

"A truly sublime artifact. A precious treasure that approaches embodying my platonic ideal of a certain special kind of movie. More than almost any other movie in recent memory, it felt like something that had crawled out of my monstercozy dreams into actual, factual reality. I was transfixed in a kind of awe." - Claire Diane

films.title: Ringu
films.description: When Hideo Nakata’s Ringu first appeared in 1998, it somehow broke containment into the West and spread like a virus, kicking off what would become the J-Horror boom. It’s fitting then that this, the proverbial OG, is about the distribution of a deadly videotape that brings about the wrath of a ghostly little girl who kills anyone who watches it (note to horror movie protagonists: don’t go looking for stuff! You’ll find it). Ringu’s themes of social disconnection and technology in conflict with the resentful past still resonate, but today the VHS vector plays differently, almost as analog’s final assault, angry for being discarded just like the film’s spectral killer.

films.title: Salome's Last Dance
films.description:
Presented by SIFF and Seattle Opera, in conjunction with their production of "Salome."

On Guy Fawkes Night, Oscar Wilde goes to a luxury brothel where the owner has prepared a surprise for the renowned author: a private and very special performance of his banned play "Salome."

films.title: Scare Package (Shorts)
films.description:
Destiny and desire lead us to nightmarish worlds. A complete package of shorts that delve into body horror, camp, psychosexual fantasy, and the grotesque.

CW: Blood / Gore

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Burning of a Family Tree (Alison Mattingly, United States, 12m)

When Eden returns home to their estranged family after the death of their abusive father, they are forced to confront their traumatic past… and their father’s reanimated corpse.

CW: Religious psychosis

CHASER (Jesse Williams, United Kingdom, 10m)

When Sophia, a trans woman on a night out crosses paths with the seemingly charming Callum, she realizes he may not have her best interest at heart…

CW: Flashing lights

The Dysphoria (Kylie Aoibheann, Australia, 13m)

A trans woman performs a satanic ritual to get a vagina, but unwittingly invites a demonic presence into her home who demands a terrible sacrifice.

Autonecrophile: What It Is To Be An Exquisite Corpse (Maxine Sizemore, United States, 11m)

Based on the filmmakers experience of OCD induced Cotard syndrome, Autonecrophile is an experimental horror short told from the perspective of a conscious dead body who gains the memories of the necrophiliac ex boyfriend who killed her, finding she died long before she wound up in her coffin.

CW: Cancer, necrophilia

Dahlia Has a Phobia (Lenox Myette, United States, 14m)

Two women retreat for a quiet weekend to salvage their unraveling relationship. But when one’s crippling fear of scarecrows resurfaces, their fragile dynamic begins to fracture.

CW: Relational abuse

God Hates a Coward (David Leo, United States, 11m)

A young transgender man goes into a psychosexual spiral after meeting the object of his desires: an aging punk vocalist.

CW: Flashing lights, sexual violence, transphobia

Resurrect Me as a Parasite (Lou Lou Sainsbury & Gabi Dao, Netherlands, 10m)

A vampiric trio facilitates the transition of a new host across a former limestone quarry and the sacred mountain grotto of Mary Magdalene, troubling the binaries of life, death, gender and parasitism.

films.title: Scary Movie
films.description: This film fearlessly spoofs popular movies and trends, delivering a rapid-fire barrage of jokes inspired by Scream, The Sixth Sense, The Matrix, I Know What You Did Last Summer, and The Blair Witch Project. It lampoons familiar teen movie tropes and memorable moments from recent films, television shows, and commercials, pushing the boundaries of parody with a no-holds-barred approach.

films.title: Screamplay
films.description:
“…takes HOLLYWOOD by the throat and STRANGLES it!”

Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies… only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (George Kuchar) instead. When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad.

Inventively produced using a host of early cinematic techniques and featuring a memorable performance by underground film legend George Kuchar, Rufus Butler Seder’s Screamplay is a singularly charming tribute to Old Hollywood and a marvel of low-budget but high-concept filmmaking. New 4K restoration by Muscle Distribution in association with Matchbox Cine.

films.title: Seattle Film Society In Focus: Tyler Michael James
films.description:
The Seattle Film Society's IN FOCUS showcase series returns this October with a screening of Tyler Michael James’s 2022 thriller LOW LIFE!

LOW LIFE follows Benny, a small-time YouTube star who catches predators online, experiences a night from hell when he lets one of them into his own home.

LOW LIFE will be preceded by a screening of the film’s proof-of-concept short, and a conversation about James’s film & career will follow the screening. This event is presented in partnership with the Northwest Film Forum.

Thursday October 15th at the Northwest Film Forum. Doors at 6:30, Film at 7. See you at the movies!

films.title: Seattle Film Society Presents Locals Only: October 2026
films.description:
October is for terror! On tap this month are flesh eating nightmares and unexplained disappearances, unnerving polaroids and weekends gone wrong. Not to mention a freak you won’t be able to unsee. For all the horror-heads out there, this one’s for you:

- POLAROID by Joey Greene: A young man is thrust into a terrifying mystery when the Polaroid photos that he has taken reveal something that isn’t actually there. (3 Min)

- BEST FRIEND MATERIAL by Mel McCarthy & Nathan Blanchard: A guys weekend goes wrong. (15 min)

- ADHESION by Mel McCarthy & Nathan Blanchard: A vain party clown suffocates in her own flesh-eating nightmare. (4 min)

- MOTHER OF NIGHT by Mohamed Abdullahi & Rayana Mohamed: After a series of unexplained disappearances, a night-shift waitress investigates a ghostly local myth and discovers the horror may be terrifyingly real. (13 Min)

- LOOK AT THIS FREAK by Alex Furnas: A reunion of old friends is disrupted by a hated roommate and something else that’s even worse. (15 Min)

This event is presented in partnership with the Northwest Film Forum. Join us for a screening and Q&A with drinks to follow at Linda’s Tavern! See ya at the movies!

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Brother
films.description: Brother is a moving story about a woman and a family put to the test in a world of violence, unfulfilled ambitions, and mounting chaos. Fourteen-year-old Dawid takes care of his younger brother and tries to live up to his mother's expectations as she tries to break free from a toxic past and start over, without her husband, who is behind bars. Although the boy has talent and strength, it becomes increasingly difficult for him to stay in control amid a daily life stretched between school, home, and the street. Everything becomes even more complicated when Konrad enters their lives, the only adult Dawid truly trusts. But this is only the beginning of turbulent events that could ultimately tear this family apart... or save it.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Erupcja
films.description: A romantic vacation goes awry when a volcanic eruption strands Bethany and her soon-to-be fiancé, Rob in Warsaw, Poland. Bethany takes the explosive event as a sign to ditch her baggage, reunite with childhood friend Nel and traipse across lofts, clubs and back alleys, all the while becoming entangled in an emotional web that challenges her sense of self. From American maverick Pete Ohs, who wrote, directed, edited, photographed, and produced this dizzyingly charming European postcard, comes Erupcja, a delightful anti-romantic comedy about the pains and pleasures of being in love.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Gorky Resort
films.description:
It is 1939. The world is descending into chaos. Thousands of Poland's most distinguished citizens are taken captive by the Soviet Union, where they are subjected to relentless ideological indoctrination as part of a larger plan.

An ambitious Soviet agent makes it his personal mission to break the will of one particular prisoner, a world-renowned young pianist and respected leader among his fellow captives. If he can be forced to surrender his convictions, many others may follow.
Can the young officer, devoted husband, and loving father withstand an opponent backed by the full power and ruthless machinery of the Soviet regime?

A deadly psychological battle begins, driven by manipulation, intimidation, and false promises. Some prisoners cling to the hope that they will soon return home. Others, convinced the enemy will show no mercy, risk everything in a desperate escape attempt. Unaware that time is running out, they do not realize that their captor is preparing to make his final move at any moment.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: GSF Shorts
films.description:
Sara has a bright future ahead with her wonderful boyfriend. On this beautiful day, they are set to celebrate their engagement at his family home. However, the accidental death of a stranger turns this special day into a nightmare. Caught in the whirlwind of tragedy, Sara faces a moral dilemma. She reluctantly becomes entangled in the family's manipulations and lies to protect them, but the bitter taste of deceit starts to weigh heavily on her. As secrets unravel, Sara discovers that the truth is far more dangerous than she imagined, forcing her to confront the dark side of the people she thought she knew. Who can she trust when the line between loyalty and betrayal blurs?

The Color of Cherries

After the death of their mother, two sisters meet in their old family home in the countryside. One’s return after years of absence becomes an opportunity to confront a difficult past marked by violence and family secrets. An intimate family drama set within the stifling space of a rural household. Their encounter is not a forced reconciliation, but an attempt to reconfigure the past and acknowledge the coexistence of conflicting personal narratives.

Fear

Jola is a taxi driver and widow, who lives with her 25-year-old son, Marek in a small town near Polish-Belarusian border. Initially disconnected from the unfolding tragedy at the border, Jola's perspective shifts dramatically after she encounters in a forest an exhausted couple with their deceased newborn. Determined to help them despite the legal risks and the strain on her relationship with her son, Jola unwittingly becomes embroiled in a situation that will irrevocably alter her life.

Penguin Habits

"Mom saves penguins" – that’s how Emilia’s job would be described by her son, Antek. The day has come for Emilia to depart for a research station in Antarctica, and the boy must stay at home under his grandfather’s care. As events begin to spiral out of control, Emilia is faced with a difficult dilemma – can she balance her dreams and professional ambitions with being a mother?

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Heel
films.description: At nineteen, Tommy is a criminal who revels in his lifestyle, orchestrating brutal acts of violence alongside his crew. That life is upended the night a stranger named Chris abducts him. He wakes up chained in the basement of a remote house, thrust into the middle of a deeply unsettling family dynamic, Chris and his enigmatic wife, Kathryn, are determined to reform him into their idea of a "good boy" through a twisted process of forced rehabilitation. Amid the confusion and fear, one thing remains clear to Tommy: he has to get out.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Home Sweet Home
films.description: When Gośka meets Grzesiek online, she's convinced he's finally The One. Grzesiek is crazy about her, showers her with flowers, and proposes in Venice. This must be love, right? But cracks quickly begin to appear in this perfect picture. Soon, their shared home becomes the most dangerous place for Gośka. Smarzowski takes a look inside "good homes," where things happen that most people prefer to keep silent about. Home Sweet Home is a film about the limits of love that you won't be able to forget.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Larp
films.description: Sergiusz, a teenager at a technical high school, is misunderstood by his family and bullied by his peers because of his passion for fantasy and LARP (live action role-playing) games. In the incredible world of imagination and adventures full of magic and swords, he's a true hero : masculine, brave, invincible. In the real world - not so much. The situation gets even more complicated when a new student joins his class, the beautiful Helena, whom he falls in love with at first sight. Unfortunately, the girl starts hanging out with a group of popular students. Sergiusz feels that, up against the school trolls, he has little chance of winning Helena's heart. Everything changes when he unexpectedly discovers the teenage girl's secret, and a famous bestselling author arrives in town.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Picasso's Mermaid
films.description: Mary accidentally discovers a Mermaid drawn on the wall of her small apartment in Warsaw. It turns out it was drawn by Pablo Picasso during his visit in 1948! The woman is delighted, but she has no idea that the Mermaid is about to turn her life upside down. Next door lives Radomski, an elderly man and retired journalist who remembers Picasso's visit. He is not at all pleased by the discovery of the Mermaid. Things from the past come back to him, mostly things he had already managed to forget. His thoughts return to Picasso's visit, as well as to the fate of the neighbors who, in exchange for the apartment they were given, had to show the Mermaid to anyone interested.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: The Altar Boys
films.description: A group of teenage altar boys, frustrated by the indifferent attitude of adults and the Church as an institution toward social injustice, decide to carry out their own unconventional plan for moral renewal. Armed with youthful rebellion and their own interpretation of Scripture, they plant a bug... in the confessional, to get to know their neighbors better. Masked like Zorro and with ambitions on the scale of Robin Hood, they become judges in their own neighborhood, helping those in need and dispensing punishment for sins. But their mission turns into a dangerous game, and as the boys apply their own idealistic code of honor, they start walking a fine line between good and evil. The real life of the housing estate blends with a mission straight out of a superhero comic book, except instead of capes, these heroes wear surplices.

films.title: Seattle Polish Film Festival: Wild, Wild East
films.description: A harsh winter in 1943. Wolff, a mysterious official from Berlin, arrives in a sleepy small town in eastern Poland. He carefully guards the reasons for his visit, but his mere presence quickly disturbs the peace in Małe Zalesie. An atmosphere of distrust and threat builds. Everyone has their own secrets, and rumors of missing gold cause the line between truth and lies to blur. A story of people caught up in dramatic choices, where life is at stake and every decision carries real consequences.

films.title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
films.description: On Halloween Eve at Mossy Bottom Farm, excitement turns to dismay when the clumsy Farmer ruins the pumpkin patch. Shaun tries fixing it with science experiments, but things go wrong when a wild beast appears in the woods.

films.title: Shrek the Musical
films.description: Shrek the Musical is a one-of-a-kind, hilarious fairy tale in which curses are reversed, monsters get the girls, donkeys and dragons find love, and princesses are beautiful in all shapes and sizes. Grumpy, gruff, green ogre Shrek lives alone in his swamp. The world is fearful and mocking of him, and he is more than happy to leave the world to itself, in turn. Suddenly, his hermit existence is thrown open, when a group of homeless fairy tale characters — Pinocchio, the Gingerbread Man, the Three Little Pigs, and more — burst upon his swamp, seeking refuge from the persecution of the cruel, vertically-challenged Lord Farquaad

films.title: Singin' in the Rain
films.description: Gene Kelly, Debbie Reynolds and Donald O'Connor star in one of the greatest musicals ever filmed. Musician Don Lockwood (Kelly) rises to stardom during Hollywood's silent-movie era--paired with the beautiful, jealous and dumb Lina Lamont (Jean Hagen). When Lockwood becomes attracted to young studio singer Kathy Selden (Reynolds), Lamont has her fired. But with the introduction of talking pictures, audiences laugh when they hear Lockwood speak for the first time--and the studio uses Selden to dub her voice. Set during the advent of "talkies," this film classic song-and-dance numbers celebrate the beginning of movie musicals.

films.title: Sleepy Hollow
films.description: Loosely based on Washington Irving's 18th-century horror tale, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, Burton's movie follows a mild-mannered detective named Ichabod Crane (Johnny Depp) in 1799, who is sent to the small town of Sleepy Hollow to investigate a series of supernatural murders.

films.title: Spookies
films.description:
“A surreal blitz of ooze, slime, hoboes, failed birthday parties, Grim Reapers, explosions, zombies, people jumping through walls, and a guy with his own face silkscreened on his shirt.” — Joseph A. Ziemba, BLEEDING SKULL!

After taking shelter in a spooky old mansion, a group of travelers discover a ouija board and decide to spend the night. But they soon learn that playing with the forces of black magic isn't fun and games, and it's not long before they're battling demonic creatures, shape shifters, and other forms of evil! Of all of the bizarre horror films made in the 1980s, SPOOKIES easily ranks among the weirdest. The film became a fan favorite thanks to its expertly rendered creature effects and notorious for its bizarre production history in which its original creators were fired and replaced by Eugenie Joseph, who added new scenes and re-edited the previously shot footage. Newly restored in 4K from its long lost original negative, SPOOKIES has never looked better.

films.title: Star Trek 2009
films.description: A young and untested crew sets out on the inaugural voyage of the U.S.S. Enterprise, the most advanced starship ever built. Led by James T. Kirk, a spirited and unconventional officer, and his logical Vulcan first officer, Spock, the crew encounters unexpected dangers and conflicts. They must overcome their personal differences and work together to navigate uncharted territory, forming a lasting camaraderie as they explore the galaxy and push the boundaries of human understanding.

films.title: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
films.description: Admiral Kirk's midlife crisis is interrupted by the return of an old enemy looking for revenge and a potentially destructive device.

films.title: Star Trek: The Motion Picture
films.description: When a destructive space entity is spotted approaching Earth, Admiral Kirk resumes command of the Starship Enterprise in order to intercept, examine, and hopefully stop it.

films.title: Stolen Kisses
films.description: As one of his film titles says, François Truffaut is The Man Who Loved Women. He reveres female beauty, intelligence, spirit, wit, and “superior understanding of emotions.” In his films, “Are women magic?” is a recurrent theme. In Truffaut’s Jules and Jim, two men initially see Jeanne Moreau’s Catherine as a statue come to life, but they soon experience her full human complexity. In Stolen Kisses, Truffaut’s cinematic alter-ego, Antoine Doinel (Jean-Pierre Léaud), a romantic who’s endearingly hapless, gains access to the hearts of Paris by taking a detective job. His touching and comic personal private investigations are the most revealing. He’s had a fluctuating romance with violinist Christine (Claude Jade): they never want each other at the same time, but both are still in the game. Antoine is hired by businessman Tabard (Michel Lonsdale) to discover why no one likes him, and is instantly smitten by the man’s elegant wife Fabienne (Delphine Seyrig, a classic New Wave woman). Following the French tradition of an older women giving a younger man his emotional education, she tells the starry-eyed Antoine, “I am not an apparition. I am a woman, unique and irreplaceable.” Meanwhile, young Christine learns that in order to get what you want in life, sometimes you have to give a push.

films.title: Sweeney Todd
films.description: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a “dark operetta” that tells the story of a London barber who seeks revenge on the judge who destroyed his life. Partnering up with Mrs Lovett, owner of the pie shop downstairs, Sweeney slaughters his customers and turns them into pies.

films.title: Take Me Home
films.description: Anna, a 38-year-old Korean adoptee with a cognitive disability, cares for her aging parents in a fragile balance of meeting each others’ needs. When a Florida heat wave shatters their family and Anna’s routine, her future is uncertain - until she creates a world where she can thrive.

films.title: Television Terror Triple Feature Pizza Party 2
films.description:
We invite you once again to make the theater your living room for another trip back in time to the heyday of made-for-TV horror movies.

For this year's triple feature pizza party, we're broadcasting three more chilling tales straight from 1960s, 70s, and 80s network TV, when original horror movies haunted home television screens on a regular basis. The evening's program consists of another trio of lesser-known gems, this time featuring creepy phone calls, stalkers, highway horror, and mysterious items of the occult. As always, the titles are secret, so you won't find out what frightening fables are in store for you until airtime.

Regular concessions will be available for purchase at the beginning of the transmission and throughout the night. The main course will arrive following the first feature. And in addition to satiating the more carnivorous appetites, we’ll have options for our vegetarian and vegan friends too. Plus, during intermissions, you’ll be treated to period-specific Halloween commercials to complete the experience.

films.title: Tenzing
films.description: Based on true events, “Tenzing” chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), became the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling. Directed by award-winning filmmaker Jennifer Peedom, “Tenzing” is a story of greatness that refuses to be diminished — and the love that makes it possible.

films.title: The Birch Wood
films.description: Young Stanislaw, riddled with tuberculosis, departs Switzerland to spend his final days with his introverted forester brother Boleshaw on their secluded farm. This return home reignites a sensual passion for life, music, and love, giving him a vibrant energy at odds with his mournful brother. Their conflicting emotions lead to confronting repressed guilt and reconciliation of the past. Set in the early 1930s, this intimate character study offered Wajda the opportunity to explore areas outside of his intensely political war films and contemplate nature through reworking motifs from classic Polish landscape and symbolist paintings in this elegant depiction of early twentieth century provincial life.

films.title: The Blue Rose: Part II
films.description: "Hang onto your light" as we jump head first into the dark nightmare of The Blue Rose. Someone or something is coming out of the forest wrecking havoc in Twin Peaks. The sheriff station is in shambles, the FBI are in over their heads and a darkness is engulfing the small mountain town. Uncover the mystery of the woods and bare witness to a nightmarish homage to David Lynch and the world of "Twin Peaks".

films.title: The Case of the Three Sided Dream
films.description:
The documentary film on the life and legacy of Rahsaan Roland Kirk – a one of a kind musician, personality, activist and windmill slayer who despite being blind, becoming paralyzed, and facing America’s racial injustices – did not relent.

Co-Presented with Earshot Jazz Festival!

films.title: The Daytrippers
films.description:
With its droll humor and bittersweet emotional heft, the feature debut of writer-director Greg Mottola announced the arrival of an unassumingly sharp-witted new talent on the 1990s indie film scene. When she discovers a love letter written to her husband (Stanley Tucci) by an unknown paramour, the distraught Eliza (Hope Davis) turns to her tight-knit Long Island family for advice. Soon the entire clan—strong-willed mom (Anne Meara), taciturn dad (Pat McNamara), and jaded sister (Parker Posey) with pretentious boyfriend (Liev Schreiber) in tow—has squeezed into a station wagon and headed into Manhattan to find out the truth, kicking off a one-crazy-day odyssey full of unexpected detours and life-changing revelations. Performed with deadpan virtuosity by a top-flight ensemble cast, The Daytrippers is a wry and piercing look at family bonds stretched to the breaking point.

Screening as a part of our quarterly Staff Selects series! This film was chosen and presented by Camille Hermida-Fuentes, our Director of Operations!

films.title: The Devils
films.description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption –and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

films.title: The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie
films.description: Luis Buñuel orchestrates consistent unpredictability through narrative pivots and tonal shifts in his satirical masterpiece that won France an Oscar for International Feature Film and received a nomination for Original Screenplay, co-written by Jean-Claude Carrière. A series of happenings sewn together amid a relatively consistent motif is driven by the six French bourgeois who persistently pursue a dinner plan that is repeatedly interrupted by random incidents. In this repetitive digression, the value of the earnest pursuit becomes trivial, exposing the absurdity of the characters’ thoughtless actions. — Academy Museum of Motion Pictures

films.title: The History of Concrete
films.description: Following the finale of his acclaimed HBO series How To with John Wilson, NYC documentarian John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world’s most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to tell this seemingly drab story and increase his movie’s appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble—literally and figuratively—as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry.

films.title: The Hitcher
films.description:
“What do you want?”
"I want you to stop me."

On a dark and stormy night, a fatigued Jim Halsey (C. Thomas Howell), driving cross country from Chicago to deliver a luxury vehicle to its San Diego owner, decides to pick up a mysterious hitchhiker (Rutger Hauer) in West Texas. Hoping for light conversation to fend off drowsiness, Jim ends up with much more than he bargained for: a psychotic killer who whips out a switchblade and dares Jim to stop his killing spree. What follows is a relentlessly sadistic cat-and-mouse nightmare under the unforgiving sun of the American Southwest. Director Robert Harmon utilizes surreal, nightmarish dream logic within the genre framework to deranged ends, putting Jim and his companion Nash (Jennfier Jason Leigh) through the ringer in high gear. The wide open vistas of the desert have never felt so isolating.

35mm print from a private collection.

films.title: The Leopard Man
films.description:
A black leopard escapes into the night, a small New Mexico town grows frightened, and Val Lewton and Jacques Tourneur have everything they need. Adapted from Cornell Woolrich’s Black Alibi and given its wonderfully lurid title by RKO in the wake of CAT PEOPLE, THE LEOPARD MAN turns a simple pulp premise into one of the strangest and most beautifully controlled thrillers of the 1940s—a movie built from darkness, sound, chance and the fear of being alone at exactly the wrong moment.

The final collaboration between Lewton and Tourneur keeps wandering away from the path a conventional mystery might take, following the nighttime life of the town with an almost dreamlike freedom. Ordinary errands and encounters acquire an inexplicable tension. Wind moves through empty streets. Water drips beneath a railroad trestle. Castanets click somewhere in the darkness. Tourneur and cinematographer Robert De Grasse fill the screen with pools of black so deep that simply waiting to discover what might emerge from them becomes almost unbearable, while the soundtrack makes every footstep and distant noise feel potentially significant.

At barely over an hour, THE LEOPARD MAN is lean enough to qualify as pure pulp and strange enough to continually escape its own premise. Beneath the mystery runs the fatalism of Woolrich and Lewton’s fascination with ordinary lives brushing unexpectedly against the unknown, all expressed through filmmaking of extraordinary economy and precision. Manny Farber was already championing it as one of Hollywood’s “original gems” in the early 1950s, and its nocturnal spell has only grown stronger with time. A street, a shadow, a sound in the distance: few horror films have ever needed less to make the darkness feel dangerous.

films.title: The Most Dangerous Game
films.description:
The Sprocket Society presents: a yacht blithely strays into cut-throat terror in this legendary pre-Code thriller, shown with spooky shorts — all on 16mm film!

A secret island owned by a rich, calculating psychopath with unholy kinks. An innocent man and woman thrown together by pure chance, stranded by “accident,” far beyond the help of any caring soul. Frayed wits and a woodsman’s knife pitted against the rich man’s cunning, his arsenal, and his pack of ravening hounds. Ah, the manhunt is on! The bloodlust…so sweet. So perfectly crafted. So inconsequential.

Joel McRae, Fay Wray, and a gloriously villainous Leslie Banks star in a tightly wound thriller that’s as short and hard-hitting as a crossbow bolt.

A low budget studio throw-away, 94 years later it’s been copied countless times yet never bested. Co-helmed by the director of King Kong and shot on the same jungle sets, the tension and fog-choked visuals linger long after the credits roll.

All aboard: your berth awaits!

Presented with selected short subjects.

films.title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
films.description: The film follows the misadventures of Jack Skellington, Halloweentown's beloved pumpkin king, who has become bored with the same annual routine of frightening people in the "real world." When Jack accidentally stumbles on Christmastown, all bright colors and warm spirits, he gets a new lease on life and plots to bring Christmas under his control by kidnapping Santa Claus and taking over the role. But Jack soon discovers even the best-laid plans of mice and skeleton men can go seriously awry.

films.title: The Parallax View
films.description: After a presidential candidate is assassinated, political reporter Joe Frady begins to suspect that the mysterious Parallax Corporation may be involved. As he investigates, others who share his suspicions start turning up dead, including his editor, Bill Rintels. Eventually, Frady uncovers a conspiracy bigger than anyone expected and must race to prevent the corporation’s next big hit as this political thriller plays out in an explosive game of cat and mouse.

films.title: The Passenger
films.description:
“What are you running away from?”
“Turn your back to the front seat.”

Lost amidst the deserts of Northern Chad, disaffected American journalist David Locke (Jack Nicholson) stumbles across the dead body of a fellow hotel acquaintance and decides to leave behind more than his sand trapped Land Rover: swapping passports, Locke abandons his identity. Renting a car “for the rest of my life” and embarking on a journey through Germany, England, and Spain, Locke soon discovers that the life he traded in for has direct connections to secret proxy wars and the international arms trade. Accompanied by a young tourist he meets in Barcelona (Maria Schneider), Locke drives further away from himself and the world while being pursued by mysterious criminals and police alike. A maestro of cinematic alienation, Michelangelo Antonioni navigates the slippery nature of identity with impeccable formal control accompanied by a career high point from Jack Nicholson.

“See the film twice and you see two films. See it a third and you see a third. So it goes.” — Robert Koehler, CinemaScope

35mm print courtesy of Sony Pictures Classics

films.title: The Phantom of the Opera
films.description:
A young soprano becomes the obsession of a disfigured and murderous musical genius who lives beneath the Paris Opéra House.

Every movie starts with a story at the North Bend Theatre. Just prior to each of the Love & War movies, our resident film experts, Kevin & Beth, will share the amazing stories behind these great films, giving you a whole new way to connect to the movie.

films.title: The Promised Land
films.description: Set during the Industrial Revolution in 19th century Łódź, three entrepreneurial friends pool their resources to open a textile factory. But friendships, personal relationships and moral values are soon tested when they encounter ruthlessly competitive barons and competing self interests. An adaptation of Nobel Prize-winning author Stanisław Reymont’s novel, the film is a compelling and continually pertinent indictment of rampant capitalism and humanity’s more selfish impulses. Wajda’s first Academy Award-nominated drama remains one of his most celebrated films.

films.title: The Ring
films.description: It sounded like just another urban legend--videotape filled with nightmarish images, leading to a phone call foretelling the viewer's death in exactly seven days. As a newspaper reporter, Rachel Keller was naturally skeptical of the story, until four teenagers all met with mysterious deaths exactly one week after watching just such a tape. Allowing her investigative curiosity to get the better of her, Rachel tracks down the video... and watches it. Now she has just seven days to unravel the mystery of the "Ring."

films.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
films.description:
Rocky Horror is back at the North Bend Theatre!

In this cult classic, sweethearts Brad (Barry Bostwick) and Janet (Susan Sarandon), stuck with a flat tire during a storm, discover the eerie mansion of Dr. Frank-N-Furter (Tim Curry), a transvestite scientist. As their innocence is lost, Brad and Janet meet a houseful of wild characters, including a rocking biker (Meat Loaf) and a creepy butler (Richard O'Brien). Through elaborate dances and rock songs, Frank-N-Furter unveils his latest creation: a muscular man named "Rocky."

films.title: The Room
films.description: The unstoppable cult classic returns for it's monthly screening! Director/Writer/Producer/Leading Man Tommy Wiseau plays Johnny, a banker who likes to throw footballs with friends, mentors a drug dealing man child, loves doggies, and isn't aware that his best friend is sleeping with his future wife. Also, he did not hit her. He did naaaaaaat. Show up early for pre-show fun.

films.title: The Scout
films.description:
Sofia works as a location scout for a TV pilot filming in New York City. It’s her job to find the homes, businesses, and exteriors where the show will be filmed. Driving around the city's different neighborhoods, she enters the private spaces of strangers to photograph their cozy apartments and eclectic shops, stepping into the fabric of their lives while trying to satisfy the demands of her erratic employers. Over a day filled with these encounters, Sofia witnesses moments of curiosity, vulnerability, and quiet tension until her work takes a sudden, personal turn. Drawing from her own experience as a location scout, writer-director Paula González-Nasser captures the poetry and costs of being a young creative. Her celebrated directorial debut The Scout crafts a contemplative exploration of urban disconnection, following one woman's journey through other people's worlds as she struggles to find her own.

Alumni of the 2016 edition of NFFTY, filmmakers Paula González-Nasser and Ryan Martin Brown will be in conversation with NFFTY Program Manager Amy Williams following the film. Special youth pricing (24 & younger) is available for the 10/9 screening.

films.title: The Shining
films.description: A struggling writer, Jack Torrance, accepts a winter caretaker position at the isolated Overlook Hotel in the Colorado Rockies, hoping the solitude will overcome his writer's block. He brings his wife, Wendy, and their young son, Danny. However, the hotel harbors a dark history, and as Jack becomes increasingly isolated by the heavy snowfall, he slowly descends into madness, threatening his family and uncovering terrifying secrets within the Overlook's walls

films.title: The Social Reckoning
films.description: Inspired by true events and the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we’re seeing play out today, this Aaron Sorkin original screenplay is a companion piece to the hit film The Social Network and a true David and Goliath story. Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help ofJeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

films.title: The Totally Halloween Sing Along
films.description:
This is Halloween; everybody make a scene.

It's a night of your favorite spooky songs and deathly dance hits, all with the lyrics on the big scream screen. Come in costume or come as you are for a monsterously good time, for no mere mortal can resist an evening of the Sing Along...

films.title: The Vanishing
films.description:
A young Dutch couple stops at a crowded highway service station in France. Saskia goes inside to buy drinks and never comes back. From that frighteningly simple premise, George Sluizer builds one of the most unnerving thrillers ever made—a movie that can turn a gas station in broad daylight into a place you’ll never quite trust again.

THE VANISHING is a marvel of restraint, stripping away nearly everything we expect a thriller to use for suspense. Sluizer doesn’t even hide the man responsible. Instead, we watch Raymond—an ordinary husband, father and chemistry teacher—rehearse conversations, measure time with a stopwatch and methodically prepare for an unspeakable act. Bernard-Pierre Donnadieu’s astonishingly matter-of-fact performance makes him more disturbing with every mundane detail, while Sluizer finds menace in cars, coffee, coins, parking lots and vacation homes. There are no monsters here, no elaborate shocks and almost no violence. There is simply the growing realization that something horrifying can happen in the middle of an ordinary day and leave behind nothing but a question.

Three years after Saskia disappears, Rex still needs the answer to that question. Soon we do too. That shared need to know is where THE VANISHING becomes truly merciless, tightening curiosity into dread with the precision of a trap closing one click at a time. Stanley Kubrick was reportedly so disturbed and fascinated by the film that he contacted Sluizer to discuss how it worked, and its reputation has only grown since. Cold without being clinical, psychologically acute without becoming cerebral, THE VANISHING is the rare thriller whose power comes not from what it hides, but from how desperately it makes you want to see it.

films.title: The Way Out
films.description: The Way Out drops you right into the action across the globe, from heavy Alaskan spine lines to local backyard laps in Whistler. The Way Out represents a path toward total freedom. Whether tracking Hoji, Chris Rubens, and Mark Abma across the iconic Swiss Alps or capturing breakout skier Lucy Leishman storming through Japan’s deep powder with three legendary freeskiers, the verdict is simple: the soul of skiing isn’t dead; it's alive and well wherever the snow is falling.

films.title: The Wedding
films.description: An intellectual poet and peasant woman unite in matrimony, with their wedding party attended by a class-crossing assortment of society. However, the veneer of harmony is broken when ghosts – drawn from local history and legend – appear out of the fog to the revellers.
