Wajda’s psychedelic adaptation of Stanisław Wyspiański’s influential 1901 play where (as stated in the prologue) “everything in [the] story is true —even the dreams,” employs dizzying cinematography and creates an eerie atmosphere to offer a searing critique of the nation’s phantoms. It became one of the most culturally significant works of Polish cinema.

films.title: Train to Busan
films.description:
Seok-woo is a workaholic dad who has trouble bonding with his young daughter Su-an. For her birthday, she wants to visit her mother in Busan. After seeing how he's been neglecting her feelings, he agrees and accompanies her on the train ride across the country.

Then, the world falls apart.

And Seok-woo transforms from an absent father to a devoted dad with one mission: to make sure his daughter survives.

Met with worldwide acclaim, Train To Busan balances a cast of well-rounded characters with suspense and bursts of visceral action, all while weaving in social commentary for a refreshing take on the zombie genre.

Presented in the original Korean language with English subtitles.

films.title: Trans Panic!
films.description:
A Christian trans hyperpop musician teams up with an intersex incel filmmaker on a mad plan involving performative terrorism, career-launching martyrdom, and a chaotic love triangle that might include JD Vance. This film asks: What if your intersectionality intersected with evil and made you suck a lot?

CW: Flashing lights

films.title: Trans-It (Shorts)
films.description:
The mode in which we journey from one place to another, physically and emotionally. Public transport, psychic transferrence, and personal transmutation. All aboard!

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Mascott (Marilyne Lamontagne, Canada, 13m)

A struggling transgender actor lands a bear mascot role on a children’s TV show, but as fame, hyper-masculinity, and public expectations close in, the bear suit refuses to come off.

As the time might be now (Noah Mancini, Zuma Link, Brazil, 16m)

On a feverish night, Dama da Noite crosses the city carrying a deck of cards that could change her fate. Between picturesque bars, collapsing apartments, and unlikely encounters, her path crosses with Onça, a young man adrift through the night.

How to Become Transgender In Order to Dodge the American Military Draft (Dustin Wilson V, Joschua Stice, United States, 6m)

Follows the creation and distribution of a flyer, instructing the residents of Seattle on how to dodge the draft.

How to Find a Career That Loves You Back (Ethernet Wang, United States, 25m)

Khloe, an isolated young trans woman, works for Scryr, a defense-technology startup that uses AI to militarize surveillance. Khloe questions the violence of her work, and as intrusive thoughts become intolerable, a decision presents itself.

Metamórfike (LUI NASCIMENTO, Brazil, 15m)

Lolo is a young non-binary person, influencer, and music video director who works as a delivery rider around the city. After receiving a mysterious delivery, strange things begin. A tropical queer sci-fi through the streets of Belo Horizonte, Brazil.

They Persist (Lachlan Salvestro, Australia, 8m)

A short film about the forever stagnant versions of ourselves that exist in the hearts and minds of the people we’ve left behind, as we grow and move on with our lives.

They Persist (Lachlan Salvestro, Australia, 8m)

A short film about the forever stagnant versions of ourselves that exist in the hearts and minds of the people we’ve left behind, as we grow and move on with our lives.

While construction is in progress, shops will remain open (Mordred Guadagno, France, 2m)

Between 2021 and 2025, a city was under massive construction preparing for a new streetcar line. As work finally come to an end, a parallel construction of the self is grappled with.

films.title: TV Party: Doomed Occult Detectives
films.description:
For a brief, beautiful period in the ’60s and ’70s, television kept trying to invent the guy you called when the police couldn’t help. Ghost hunters, psychic investigators, demonologists, and occult experts armed with ancient books, skeptical assistants and suspiciously helpful police contacts, they were built to spend every week cracking another impossible case. Before KOLCHAK went chasing monsters through the night and long before THE X-FILES put the paranormal on the federal payroll, these would-be series were already trying to turn the venerable occult detective of weird fiction into a weekly television hero. Networks commissioned the pilots, watched them…and repeatedly decided there would be no Episode Two.

TV PARTY exhumes two of the best surviving specimens: a mystery double feature of orphaned pilots from series that never existed, each introducing a brand-new supernatural sleuth and sending him straight into his first—and last—case. Expect haunted houses, impossible murders, forbidden artifacts, black magic and two tantalizing glimpses of the horror shows television almost gave us. No titles until showtime. The networks buried them. We’re putting them back on the air.

films.title: Two-Lane Blacktop
films.description:
An unnamed drag racing duo (James Taylor and "The Beach Boys"' Dennis Wilson, referred to as The Driver and Mechanic in novelist Rudy Wurlitzer’s screenplay) head eastward from Los Angeles in their souped up ‘55 Chevy. They cross paths with an orbit-orange GTO and its wandering loner of a driver played by Warren Oates, bedecked throughout in a kaleidoscope wardrobe of cashmere sweaters. Vying for the attention of a restless hitchhiker in tow (Laurie Bird), the trio embark on a race for pink slips across six southern states. Filmed in sequence and entirely on location, Monte Hellman’s low budget masterpiece of highway philosophy features gorgeous widescreen photography and sparse, existential dialogue that captures a moment in time when, as Vincent Canby states, “faith in God is a lot less important, less immediate and even less mystical than faith in the internal combustion engine.” The quintessential American road film.

“In Two-Lane Blacktop [the road] becomes something altogether different and far more interesting: a repository of dreams and fantasies, for squares, hipsters, and obsessives alike…It is a movie about loneliness, and the attempts made by people to connect with one another and maintain their solitude at the same time—an impossible task, an elusive dream.” — Kent Jones

35mm print courtesy of Universal

films.title: Understanding Myself as an Amphibian
films.description:
Understanding Myself as an Amphibian is a Queer ecology feature documentary exploring sexual diversity in wildlife, drawing connections between incredible species and the director’s own journey. The film is an enlightening reflection on wildlife and the influences affecting our understanding of animal and human behaviour.

Screens with the short film Objectionable Fruit!

(Hogan Seidel & Gabby Follett, United States, 15m)

Objectionable Fruit is an experimental four channel 16mm documentary short examining the Ginkgo tree—a living fossil celebrated for its resilience and unique capacity to change sexes, defying human-imposed binaries.

CW: Flashing lights

films.title: Universal Monster Mash Double Feature
films.description:
Featuring FRANKENSTEIN MEETS THE WOLF MAN and ABBOTT AND COSTELLO MEET FRANKENSTEIN!

Universal spent the 1930s turning Dracula, Frankenstein’s Monster and the Wolf Man into movie stars. Then somebody had the bright idea to start putting them in each other’s movies. This double feature catches the Universal monster rally at its beginning and its glorious peak: first the movie that brought two horror franchises crashing together, then the one that let Abbott and Costello hang out in the wreckage.

It starts with poor Larry Talbot. All the Wolf Man wants is to die. Instead, grave robbers dig him up, the full moon brings him back to life, and his search for a permanent cure leads him straight to the frozen body of Frankenstein’s Monster. FRANKENSTEIN MEETS THE WOLF MAN piles on foggy graveyards, ruined castles, terrified villagers, mad science, Bela Lugosi in neck bolts, Lon Chaney Jr. suffering beautifully and a cheerful musical number called “Life Is Short, but Death Is Long” before finally delivering on the promise of its title: two monsters beating the hell out of each other while the laboratory comes down around them.

Five years later, Universal decided what this situation needed was Lou Costello. Dracula wants his brain for Frankenstein’s Monster. The Wolf Man wants to stop Dracula. Bud Abbott doesn’t believe any of this is happening. And Bela Lugosi, returning to Dracula for the first time since 1931, treats the whole ridiculous situation with the dignity of a bloodsucking aristocrat whose evil scheme does not involve two vaudeville comedians. ABBOTT AND COSTELLO MEET FRANKENSTEIN somehow lets the monsters remain scary, Abbott and Costello remain funny, and both movies occupy the same frame without anybody blinking. Dracula turns into a bat. The Wolf Man goes through a window. Frankenstein’s Monster throws a woman out another window. And when the dust settles, Universal has somehow made one of its funniest comedies and one of its greatest monster movies at the same time.

Two movies, five years apart, tracing one of the happiest developments in horror history: Universal turning its stable of monsters into the world’s ugliest repertory company.

films.title: Verity
films.description: Lowen Ashleigh is hired by Jeremy Crawford to ghostwrite novels for his bestselling author wife Verity, who is unable to finish following an accident. Lowen gradually uncovers Verity's disturbing truths while residing at the Crawfords' home to work.

films.title: Vertigo
films.description:
James Stewart stars as a retired San Francisco detective who takes on a case to follow an old friend's wife, only to spiral deeper into an obsession with her.

Considered one of Hitchcock's finest. Stewart is in top form as he falls further into madness.

films.title: VHS Über Alles Presents...
films.description:
SHOT ON VIDEO HALLOWEEN SPECIAL!

Experience cult movies in analog glory! Seattle’s ultimate VHS screening series delivers an unstoppable onslaught of 0.5-inch magnetic power. All we can tell you about the film is this:

A HORRIFYING DESCENT INTO THE TWISTED KILLING SPREE OF A PSYCHOPATH!

Just $5 gets you a seat before we hit “play” on the all-powerful VCR.

films.title: Wagon Master
films.description:
A picaresque road poem, Wagon Master remained a personal favorite of John Ford’s amongst his own pictures and one of three that “came closest to being what I wanted to achieve.” Nearly plotless with an emphasis on grace notes, this relaxed film charts the journey of two horse traders with a shared yen for adventure who are hired by Elder Wiggs (Ward Bond) to lead a Mormon wagon train through southeastern Utah. Along the way they encounter a theater troupe, sex workers, lawmen, Indigenous peoples, and ornery outlaws on the run, all of whom find themselves brought in as members of the traveling community through what Harvard Film Archive calls an “almost musical combination, separation and recombination.” Deceptively simple and elegant in construction, Ford shot this lyrical and visually rapturous film away from his usual commanding landscapes of Monument Valley, instead emphasizing the beauty of a multicultural motley crew of outcasts on the dusty trail.

“Seldom has the western landscape seemed such a tangible emblem of hope and freedom. A masterpiece beyond question — but a masterpiece that never degenerates into pomposity or self-consciousness. It's American filmmaking at its finest and most eloquent." — Dave Kehr, Chicago Reader

“Wagon Master is more poetry than drama…less interested in where it is going (plot), than in where it is (the moment). Still, obviously, it is a movie about passage, a ‘parade’ West. Only briefly is ‘home,’ the antithesis of passage, suggested.” — Tag Gallagher

35mm print courtesy of Park Circus

films.title: Whalefall
films.description: Following the death of his father (Josh Brolin), Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams) goes diving off the central Coast of California in search of his remains, but is swallowed by a massive sperm whale. While trapped inside its belly with only one hour of oxygen left, Jay comes to realize that the hard-earned lessons his father imparted may be the key to his escape.

films.title: What the River Knows
films.description: Today, a lost Eden emerges from beneath Lake Powell, revealing both the consequences of past mistakes and the potential for a new path forward for the Colorado River. What The River Knows explores this pivotal moment, where the urgent need to rethink water management in the West aligns with an opportunity to restore a stunning landscape and flooded ancestral homeland. Amidst the grim discussions surrounding climate change and the Colorado River crisis, the film tells a powerful story of nature’s resilience: Glen Canyon is coming back to life.

films.title: Who Moves America
films.description: As the world’s largest package delivery company, UPS moves millions of packages across more than 200 countries and territories each day – and its workforce holds the power to bring that machine to a halt. Who Moves America follows a UPS driver in California casting his first strike vote, a Teamster in New York who walked the picket line during the historic 1997 strike, and a warehouse worker in Kentucky balancing night shifts with community college, weighing whether she can afford to say no, as well as access to the General President of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Sean O’Brien. As they and their co-workers organize, argue, and campaign across the country, the film builds toward a single, high-stakes vote: accept the deal, or risk everything for a strike that could reshape the American economy. Through intimate access and on-the-ground storytelling, Who Moves America reveals the human stories behind the single largest collective bargaining agreement in North America and explores the power and complexity of collective action in modern America.

films.title: Wicker
films.description: An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, Wicker tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). When her wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life.

films.title: Wildwood
films.description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

films.title: Withdrawal
films.description:
Writer/director/editor Aaron Strand scheduled to join for an in-person intro and Q&A. Raw, unflinching, and surprisingly funny, WITHDRAWAL was shot on miniDV in Athens, GA for a budget of $60k and is a prime example of indie filmmaking at its finest.

Artistic lovers Viv (Millie Rose Evans) and Jay (Brent Michal) are trapped in a vicious cycle of codependent heroin addiction. When Viv's wealthy parents hire an interventionist to take her to rehab, the couple decides to go it alone with nothing but a suboxone prescription and each other. All they have to do is survive one harrowing night of withdrawal. As the hours tick by, physical, mental, and emotional torments send them searching through fractured memories, trying to figure out where it all went wrong.

Winner of a dozen awards on the festival circuit, including Best Feature/Best Director at the Art of Brooklyn Film Festival and Best Actress at the Kanazawa Film Festival.

films.title: You Can See Everything
films.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything.

films.title: Young Frankenstein
films.description: Following in the footsteps of his infamous grandfather, Dr. Frederick Frankenstein inherits his ancestor's Transylvanian castle and laboratory. He initially attempts to distance himself from the family's legacy, but is drawn into recreating the experiments that brought his grandfather's monster to life. With the help of Igor, the bubbly Inga, and the unsettling Frau Blücher, Frederick’s plans are complicated by a living monster and the unexpected arrival of his fiancée, Elizabeth, leading to chaotic and hilarious consequences.

films.title: Zi
films.description:
In Hong Kong, a young woman haunted by visions of her future self meets a stranger who changes the course of her night—and possibly her life. Kogonada plays with — and returns to — form in this sensitive cinematic poem. Held within a stylish jaunt through the streets of Hong Kong, zi is a film with soul and a wavelike confidence that commits to recursivity as a mode and central theme. Kogonada regulars Michelle Mao, Haley Lu Richardson, and Jin Ha carefully portray transitory misfits, grappling with a clever fusion of existential anxiety, romantic misgiving, and personal memory. Somewhere between sci-fi and supernatural, a deep, easy warmth takes root. Kogonada crafts a decidedly contained film, exploring a pervasive sense of unmooring, yet cultivating an unrelenting sense of peace. Through the igniting/smoldering embers of relationships lost/forming, zi is an invitation to surrender to Kogonada’s truly indie world of temporal fragmentation.

“An instant classic.”

— Richard Brody, The New Yorker

“Bold, beautiful, and beguiling. Michelle Mao crafts what ought to be a breakout performance for the ages.”

— Chase Hutchinson, TheWrap
